f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ [78:1]
Concerning what are they disputing? [78:1]
b: About what, about what thing, are they, the people of Quraysh, questioning one another?

f:
عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ [78:2]
Concerning the Great News, [78:2]
b: About the awesome tiding ([this is] the explication of that ‘thing’; the interrogative is meant to emphasise its magnitude) — this [awesome tiding] is the Qur’ān, comprising [news of] the Resurrection and so on, which the Prophet ﷺ (s) brought —

f:
الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ [78:3]
About which they cannot agree. [78:3]
b: concerning which they are at variance, for the believers affirm it, while the disbelievers repudiate it.

f:
كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ [78:4]
Verily, they shall soon (come to) know! [78:4]
b: No indeed! — a disavowal — they will come to know, what will befall them for their rejection of it.

f:
ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ [78:5]
Verily, verily they shall soon (come to) know! [78:5]
b: Again, no indeed! They will come to know! ([reiterated] for emphasis; thumma is added here to declare that the second threat of chastisement is more severe than the first). God, exalted be He, then alludes to His power to resurrect, saying:

f:
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا [78:6]
Have We not made the earth as a wide expanse, [78:6]
b: Have We not made the earth a cradle, a bed, like a cradle,

f:
وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا [78:7]
And the mountains as pegs? [78:7]
b: and the mountains pegs?, with which the earth is tied down like tents are tied down with pegs (the interrogative is meant as an affirmative).

f:
وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا [78:8]
And (have We not) created you in pairs, [78:8]
b: And created you in pairs?, males and females,

f:
وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا [78:9]
And made your sleep for rest, [78:9]
b: and made your sleep for rest?, repose for your bodies,

f:
وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا [78:10]
And made the night as a covering, [78:10]
b: and made the night a cloak?, to cover you with its darkness,

f:
وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا [78:11]
And made the day as a means of subsistence? [78:11]
b: and made the day for livelihood?, a time for seeking livelihood,

f:
وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا [78:12]
And (have We not) built over you the seven firmaments, [78:12]
b: and built above you seven mighty ones?, seven heavens (shidād is the plural of shadīda) that is to say, strong and sturdy unaffected by the passage of time,

f:
وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا [78:13]
And placed (therein) a Light of Splendour? [78:13]
b: and set a radiant lamp?, namely, the sun,

f:
وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا [78:14]
And do We not send down from the clouds water in abundance, [78:14]
b: and sent down from the rain-clouds (mu‘sirāt), the clouds due to give rain (similar to [the term] mu‘sir, which denotes a girl nearing menstruation) cascading water?, pouring forth,

f:
لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا [78:15]
That We may produce therewith corn and vegetables, [78:15]
b: that with it We may bring forth grains, such as wheat, and plants, such as figs,

f:
وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا [78:16]
And gardens of luxurious growth? [78:16]
b: and gardens, orchards, of intertwining foliage? (alfāf is the plural of lafīf, similar [in pattern] to sharīf, ‘noble’, [plural] ashrāf).

f:
إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتًا [78:17]
Verily the Day of Sorting out is a thing appointed, [78:17]
b: Verily the Day of Decision, for creatures, is the tryst, a time [fixed] for reward and punishment,

f:
يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا [78:18]
The Day that the Trumpet shall be sounded, and ye shall come forth in crowds; [78:18]
b: the day the Trumpet, the Horn, is blown (yawma yunfakhu fī’l-sūri is either a substitution for, or an explication of, yawma’l-fasli, ‘the Day of Decision’, the blower being Isrāfīl) and you come, forth from your graves to the site [of the Resurrection], in droves, in diverse groups,

f:
وَفُتِحَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا [78:19]
And the heavens shall be opened as if there were doors, [78:19]
b: and the heaven is opened (read futtihat or futihat), sundered for the descent of the angels, and becomes as gates, it becomes [a heaven] with gates,

f:
وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا [78:20]
And the mountains shall vanish, as if they were a mirage. [78:20]
b: and the mountains are set in motion, dislocated from their positions, and become as a mirage, as fine dust, that is to say, like it in terms of its levity when in motion.

f:
إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا [78:21]
Truly Hell is as a place of ambush, [78:21]
b: Verily Hell lurks in ambush (mirsādan, in the sense of rāsidatan or mursidatan, ‘lying in wait’)

f:
لِلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا [78:22]
For the transgressors a place of destination: [78:22]
b: for the rebellious, the disbelievers, who will not be able to avoid it, [it is] a resort, a retreat for them, and so they will enter it,

f:
لَابِثِينَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا [78:23]
They will dwell therein for ages. [78:23]
b: to remain (lābithīna is an implied circumstantial qualifier, in other words, their remaining therein will be decreed [to be]) therein for ages, for endless epochs (ahqāb is the plural of huqb),

f:
لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا وَلَا شَرَابًا [78:24]
Nothing cool shall they taste therein, nor any drink, [78:24]
b: tasting in it neither coolness, [neither] sleep, [something] which they will not taste [therein], nor drink, [nor] anything that is imbibed for the sake of its delightful taste,

f:
إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا [78:25]
Save a boiling fluid and a fluid, dark, murky, intensely cold, [78:25]
b: except boiling water, of extreme temperatures, and pus (read ghasāqan or ghassāqan, which is the vile matter that is emitted by the [bodies of the] inhabitants of the Fire), which is what they will [indeed] taste. They are given this pair [of tortures],

f:
جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا [78:26]
A fitting recompense (for them). [78:26]
b: as a fitting requital, one that accords with [the nature of] their deeds, for there is no sin greater than disbelief, and no chastisement greater than the Fire.

f:
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًا [78:27]
For that they used not to fear any account (for their deeds), [78:27]
b: Indeed they never feared any reckoning, given their rejection of the Resurrection,

f:
وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّابًا [78:28]
But they (impudently) treated Our Signs as false. [78:28]
b: and they denied Our signs, the Qur’ān, mendaciously,

f:
وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَابًا [78:29]
And all things have We preserved on record. [78:29]
b: and everything, in the way of deeds, have We kept count of, have We recorded precisely, in a Book, as [individual] written records in the Preserved Tablet, in order to requite [creatures] in accordance with them, including [the record of] their denial of the Qur’ān.

f:
فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذَابًا [78:30]
"So taste ye (the fruits of your deeds); for no increase shall We grant you, except in Punishment." [78:30]
b: ‘So [now] taste! — in other words, it will be said to them in the Hereafter, when the chastisement has befallen them: taste [now] your requital! For We will increase you in nothing but chastisement’, in addition to your [due] chastisement.

f:
إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا [78:31]
Verily for the Righteous there will be a fulfilment of (the heart´s) desires; [78:31]
b: Truly for the God-fearing there will be a triumph, a place of triumph, in Paradise:

f:
حَدَائِقَ وَأَعْنَابًا [78:32]
Gardens enclosed, and grapevines; [78:32]
b: gardens, orchards (hadā’iqa is either a substitution for, or an explication of, mafāzan, ‘a triumph’) and vineyards (wa-a‘nāban is a supplement to mafāzan, ‘a triumph’),

f:
وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَابًا [78:33]
And voluptuous women of equal age; [78:33]
b: and buxom maidens (kawā‘ib is the plural of kā‘ib) of equal age (atrāb is the plural of tirb),

f:
وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا [78:34]
And a cup full (to the brim). [78:34]
b: and a brimming cup, wine filling the vessels in which it is in; in sūrat al-Qitāl [it is said], and rivers of wine [Q. 47:15].

f:
لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا وَلَا كِذَّابًا [78:35]
No vanity shall they hear therein, nor Untruth:- [78:35]
b: They will not hear in it, that is, [in] Paradise, when they drink wine and in other situations, any vain talk, any words of falsehood, or lies, between one another (read kidhāban, to mean kadhiban, ‘lies’, or kidhdhāban to mean takdhīban, ‘lying’), in contrast to what happens in this world when wine is drunk,

f:
جَزَاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا [78:36]
Recompense from thy Lord, a gift, (amply) sufficient, [78:36]
b: [this will be] a reward from your Lord, in other words, God has rewarded them with this reward as, a gift (‘atā’an substitutes for jazā’an, ‘reward’) that is sufficing, [that is] abundant (hisāban, [as meaning ‘abundant’] derives from their saying a‘tānī fa-ahsabanī, ‘he gave me so abundantly that I said, “that is enough for me”’ [hasbī]),

f:
رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمَٰنِ ۖ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًا [78:37]
(From) the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all between, (Allah) Most Gracious: None shall have power to argue with Him. [78:37]
b: [from] the Lord of the heavens and the earth (read rabbi, ‘[from] the Lord of’, or rabbu, ‘[He is] the Lord of’) and all that is between them, the Compassionate One (likewise [read rahmāni or rahmānu], or read rahmānu with rabbi [for the preceding]), Whom, exalted be He, they, that is, creatures, will not be able to address, that is to say, not one of them will be able to address Him for fear of Him,

f:
يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ صَفًّا ۖ لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَابًا [78:38]
The Day that the Spirit and the angels will stand forth in ranks, none shall speak except any who is permitted by (Allah) Most Gracious, and He will say what is right. [78:38]
b: on the day (yawma is the adverbial qualifier for lā yamlikūna, ‘they will not be able to’) when the Spirit, Gabriel عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, or God’s hosts, and the angels stand arrayed (saffan is a circumstantial qualifier, in other words, mustaffīna). They, creatures, will not speak, except him whom the Compassionate One permits, to speak, and who says what is right, from among the believers and the angels: as if [meaning] that they will intercede for he whom He approves of.

f:
ذَٰلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَقُّ ۖ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ مَآبًا [78:39]
That Day will be the sure Reality: Therefore, whoso will, let him take a (straight) return to his Lord! [78:39]
b: That is the True Day, whose coming to pass is definite, namely, the Day of Resurrection. So whoever wishes [to], let him seek resort with his Lord, a return [to Him], that is to say, [let him] return to God by being obedient to Him, so that he may be secure from chastisement in it.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا [79:1]
By the (angels) who tear out (the souls of the wicked) with violence; [79:1]
b: By those that wrest, [by] the angels who wrest the souls of disbelievers, violently;

f:
وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا [79:2]
By those who gently draw out (the souls of the blessed); [79:2]
b: by those that draw out, [by] the angels who draw out the souls of believers, gently;

f:
وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا [79:3]
And by those who glide along (on errands of mercy), [79:3]
b: by those that glide serenely, [by] the angels who descend from the heavens with His command, exalted be He;

f:
فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا [79:4]
Then press forward as in a race, [79:4]
b: by those that race forward, [by] the angels who race forward to Paradise with the souls of believers;

f:
فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا [79:5]
Then arrange to do (the Commands of their Lord), [79:5]
b: and by those that direct the affair, [by] the angels who direct the affairs of this world, that is to say, they descend with the directions for it [from God] (the response to all of these oath clauses has been omitted, understood to be [something like], la-tub‘athunna yā kuffāra Makka, ‘you shall certainly be resurrected, O disbelievers of Mecca!’, which is also the operator of [the following clause]):

f:
يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ [79:6]
One Day everything that can be in commotion will be in violent commotion, [79:6]
b: the day when the Tremor quakes, that is to say, the first blast, as a result of which everything will be shaken violently (thus it [the subject] has been described in terms of the effect it produces),

f:
تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ [79:7]
Followed by oft-repeated (commotions): [79:7]
b: and is followed by the Aftershock, the second blast; between the two [blasts] is a span of forty years (the sentence [tatba‘uhā’l-rādifatu] is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-rājifa, ‘the Tremor’, in other words, the ‘day’ can [adverbially] accommodate both blasts and other events, and so for this reason it can also properly function as the adverbial qualifier for the Resurrection that will take place after the second [blast]);

f:
قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ [79:8]
Hearts that Day will be in agitation; [79:8]
b: on that day hearts will be trembling, frightened and anxious,

f:
أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ [79:9]
Cast down will be (their owners´) eyes. [79:9]
b: their eyes humbled, abject, because of the terror that they see.

f:
يَقُولُونَ أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ [79:10]
They say (now): "What! shall we indeed be returned to (our) former state? [79:10]
b: They, those of the [mentioned] hearts and eyes, will say, mockingly and in rejection of the Resurrection: ‘Are we indeed (read a-innā pronouncing both hamzas, or by not pronouncing the second, and inserting an alif between them in both cases, and in both instances) being restored as before? Shall we be restored to life after death (al-hāfira is a noun signifying the ‘first part’ of anything, from which is derived the expression raja‘a fī hāfiratihi to mean that so and so ‘returned whence he had come’).

f:
أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا نَخِرَةً [79:11]
"What! - when we shall have become rotten bones?" [79:11]
b: What! When we have been decayed bones?’ (nakhira: a variant reading has nākhira, ‘decayed and withered’), will we have life again?

f:
قَالُوا تِلْكَ إِذًا كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ [79:12]
They say: "It would, in that case, be a return with loss!" [79:12]
b: They will say, ‘That, return of ours to life, then, if it were true, would be a ruinous return!’.

f:
فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ [79:13]
But verily, it will be but a single (Compelling) Cry, [79:13]
b: God, exalted be He, says: But it, the Aftershock, which will be followed by the Resurrection, will be only a single blast, and so when it is blasted:

f:
فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ [79:14]
When, behold, they will be in the (full) awakening (to Judgment). [79:14]
b: behold, then, they, all creatures, will be upon the surface of the earth, alive, after having been dead inside it.

f:
هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَى [79:15]
Has the story of Moses عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ reached thee? [79:15]
b: Have you, O Muhammad (s), received the story of Moses عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ (hadīthu Mūsā operates [the clause that follows]),

f:
إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى [79:16]
Behold, thy Lord did call to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa:- [79:16]
b: when his Lord called out to him in the holy valley of Tuwā? — this is the name of the valley (it may be read with nunation, Tuwan, or without) — and He said:

f:
اذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ [79:17]
"Go thou to Pharaoh for he has indeed transgressed all bounds: [79:17]
b: ‘Go to Pharaoh; he has indeed become rebellious, he has exceeded [all] bounds with his disbelief,

f:
فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلَىٰ أَنْ تَزَكَّىٰ [79:18]
"And say to him, ´Wouldst thou that thou shouldst be purified (from sin)?- [79:18]
b: and say, “Would you — I call you [to] — purify yourself (tazakkā: a variant reading has tazzakkā, where the original second tā’ [of tatazakkā] has been assimilated with the zāy), to purge yourself of idolatry, by bearing witness that there is no god but God,

f:
وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ [79:19]
"´And that I guide thee to thy Lord, so thou shouldst fear Him?´" [79:19]
b: and allow me to guide you to your Lord, to show you how to know Him (ma‘rifa) by way of proofs, so that you may have fear [of Him]?” ’

f:
فَأَرَاهُ الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرَىٰ [79:20]
Then did (Moses) show him the Great Sign. [79:20]
b: So he showed him the greatest sign, from among His nine signs, namely, the [glowing] hand or the [slithering] staff.

f:
فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَىٰ [79:21]
But (Pharaoh) rejected it and disobeyed (guidance); [79:21]
b: But he, Pharaoh, denied, Moses عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, and disobeyed, God, exalted be He.

f:
ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ [79:22]
Further, he turned his back, striving hard (against Allah). [79:22]
b: Then he turned his back, to faith, going about in haste, throughout the land causing corruption.

f:
فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَىٰ [79:23]
Then he collected (his men) and made a proclamation, [79:23]
b: Then he gathered, he assembled the sorcerers and his armies, and proclaimed,

f:
فَقَالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَىٰ [79:24]
Saying, "I am your Lord, Most High". [79:24]
b: and said, ‘I am your most high lord!’, above whom is no other lord.

f:
فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكَالَ الْآخِرَةِ وَالْأُولَىٰ [79:25]
But Allah did punish him, (and made an) example of him, - in the Hereafter, as in this life. [79:25]
b: So God seized him, He destroyed him by drowning him, as punishment for the latter, that is to say, these [last] words [of his], and for the former, that is to say, his saying previously, ‘I do not know of any god for you other than me’ [Q. 28:38] — and between the two [claims made by Pharaoh] was an interval of forty years.

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشَىٰ [79:26]
Verily in this is an instructive warning for whosoever feareth (Allah). [79:26]
b: Assuredly in that, which is mentioned, there is a moral for him who fears, God, exalted be He.

f:
أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ ۚ بَنَاهَا [79:27]
What! Are ye the more difficult to create or the heaven (above)? (Allah) hath constructed it: [79:27]
b: Are you (read a-antum pronouncing both hamzas, or by substituting an alif for the second one, not pronouncing it and inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the former, or without [this insertion]), namely, [you] the deniers of the Resurrection, harder to create or the heaven which He has built?, harder to create (banāhā: an explication of the manner of [its] creation).

f:
رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا [79:28]
On high hath He raised its canopy, and He hath given it order and perfection. [79:28]
b: He made it rise high — an explication of the manner of [its] construction; in other words, He made its vertical extension high; it is also said that samkahā means ‘its ceiling’ — and levelled it: He made it even, flawless,

f:
وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا [79:29]
Its night doth He endow with darkness, and its splendour doth He bring out (with light). [79:29]
b: and darkened its night, and brought forth its day: He exposed the light of its sun (‘night’ has been annexed to it [the heaven] because it represents its shade, and likewise the ‘sun’, because it represents its light);

f:
وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا [79:30]
And the earth, moreover, hath He extended (to a wide expanse); [79:30]
b: and after that He spread out the earth: He made it flat, for it had been created before the heaven, but without having been spread out;

f:
أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا [79:31]
He draweth out therefrom its moisture and its pasture; [79:31]
b: from it He has brought forth (akhraja: a circumstantial qualifier with a suppressed [preceding] qad, that is to say, mukhrijan, ‘bringing forth [from it]’) its waters, by making its springs gush forth, and its pastures, what cattle graze, of trees and herbage, and what humans consume of foods and fruits (the use of mar‘ā to express this [of the earth] is figurative),

f:
وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا [79:32]
And the mountains hath He firmly fixed;- [79:32]
b: and has set firm the mountains, on the face of the earth so that it stays still,

f:
مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ [79:33]
For use and convenience to you and your cattle. [79:33]
b: as a [source of] sustenance (an object denoting reason for an implied [verbal clause], in other words, fa‘ala dhālika mut‘atan or tamtī‘an, ‘He did this to provide [a source of] sustenance’) for you and your flocks (an‘ām is the plural of na‘am, which are camels, cows and sheep).

f:
فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَىٰ [79:34]
Therefore, when there comes the great, overwhelming (Event),- [79:34]
b: So when the Greatest Catastrophe befalls — the second blast —

f:
يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا سَعَىٰ [79:35]
The Day when man shall remember (all) that he strove for, [79:35]
b: the day when man will remember (yawma yatadhakkaru’l-insānu substitutes for idhā, ‘when’) his efforts, in the [life of the] world, in the way of good or evil,

f:
وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِمَنْ يَرَىٰ [79:36]
And Hell-Fire shall be placed in full view for (all) to see,- [79:36]
b: and the Hell-fire, the consuming Fire, is revealed for all to see, for every on-looker (the response to idhā, ‘when’, is [what follows]):

f:
فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغَىٰ [79:37]
Then, for such as had transgressed all bounds, [79:37]
b: as for him who was rebellious, [who] disbelieved,

f:
وَآثَرَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا [79:38]
And had preferred the life of this world, [79:38]
b: and preferred the life of this world, by pursuing [carnal] desires,

f:
فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ [79:39]
The Abode will be Hell-Fire; [79:39]
b: Hell-fire will indeed be the abode, his abode.

f:
وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ [79:40]
And for such as had entertained the fear of standing before their Lord´s (tribunal) and had restrained (their) soul from lower desires, [79:40]
b: But as for him who feared the stance before his Lord, his standing before Him, and forbade the, evil-bidding, soul from [pursuing] desire, that leads to perdition as a result of [that person’s] lusting after [carnal] desires,

f:
فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ [79:41]
Their abode will be the Garden. [79:41]
b: Paradise will indeed be the abode: in sum the response [to idhā, ‘when’, verse 34] is that the disobedient one will be in the Fire and the obedient one in Paradise.

f:
يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا [79:42]
They ask thee about the Hour,-´When will be its appointed time? [79:42]
b: They, that is, the disbelievers of Mecca, will ask you about the Hour: when will it set in?, when will it come to pass and when will it begin?

f:
فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا [79:43]
Wherein art thou (concerned) with the declaration thereof? [79:43]
b: What have you to do with the mention of it?, in other words, you have no knowledge of it in order to mention it.

f:
إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهَاهَا [79:44]
With thy Lord in the Limit fixed therefor. [79:44]
b: With your Lord it belongs ultimately, ultimate knowledge of it [lies with Him]; none other than Him has any knowledge of it.

f:
إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشَاهَا [79:45]
Thou art but a Warner for such as fear it. [79:45]
b: You are only a warner for, your warning will only benefit, the one who fears it.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ [80:1]
(The Prophet ﷺ) frowned and turned away, [80:1]
b: He, the Prophet ﷺ, frowned, glowered with his face, and turned away,

f:
أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَىٰ [80:2]
Because there came to him the blind man (interrupting). [80:2]
b: because the blind man came to him: ‘Abd Allāh son of Umm Maktūm, who interrupted him while he was busy with those notables of Quryash whose submission [to God] he was very eager for. The blind man was not aware that he was busy with these and so he called out to him, ‘Teach me of what God has taught you’. However, the Prophet ﷺ (s) went off to his house. He was then reproached for this with what was revealed in this sūra. Afterwards, whenever he came to him, the Prophet ﷺ would say to him, ‘Greetings to him on whose account God reproached me!’, and would lay down his cloak for him.

f:
وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ [80:3]
But what could tell thee but that perchance he might grow (in spiritual understanding)?- [80:3]
b: And how would you know? Perhaps he would cleanse himself (yazzakkā: the original tā’ [of yatazakkā] has been assimilated with the zāy), that is, [perhaps] he would purge himself of sins by what he hears from you,

f:
أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرَىٰ [80:4]
Or that he might receive admonition, and the teaching might profit him? [80:4]
b: or be admonished (yadhdhakkar: the original tā’ [of yatadhakkar] has been assimilated with the dhāl) and so the reminder, the admonition heard from you, might benefit him (a variant reading [for tanfa‘uhu] has tanfa‘ahu as the response to the optative statement).

f:
أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَىٰ [80:5]
As to one who regards Himself as self-sufficient, [80:5]
b: But as for the one [who thinks himself] self-sufficient, through wealth,

f:
فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ [80:6]
To him dost thou attend; [80:6]
b: to him you [do] attend (tasaddā: a variant reading has tassaddā, where the original second tā’ [of tatasaddā] has been assimilated with the sād), [him] you accept and turn your attention to;

f:
وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّىٰ [80:7]
Though it is no blame to thee if he grow not (in spiritual understanding). [80:7]
b: yet it is not your concern if he does not cleanse himself, [if he does not] believe.

f:
وَأَمَّا مَنْ جَاءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ [80:8]
But as to him who came to thee striving earnestly, [80:8]
b: But as for him who comes to you hurrying (yas‘ā is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of [the verb] jā’a, ‘comes’)

f:
وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ [80:9]
And with fear (in his heart), [80:9]
b: fearful, of God (wa-huwa yakhshā is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of [the verb] yas‘ā, ‘hurrying’) — this being the blind man —

f:
فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ [80:10]
Of him wast thou unmindful. [80:10]
b: to him you pay no heed (talahhā: the original second tā’ [of tatalahhā] has been omitted), that is to say, from him you are distracted [by other things].

f:
كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ [80:11]
By no means (should it be so)! For it is indeed a Message of instruction: [80:11]
b: No indeed!, do not behave like this. Truly it, the sūra, is, or the verses [are], a reminder, an admonition for [all] creatures —

f:
فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ [80:12]
Therefore let whoso will, keep it in remembrance. [80:12]
b: so let whoever will, remember it, preserve it [in his memory] and thus be admonished by it —

f:
فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ [80:13]
(It is) in Books held (greatly) in honour, [80:13]
b: on leaves (fī suhufin is the second predicate of innahā, ‘truly it’, and what precedes it is a parenthetical statement) [that are] honoured, by God,

f:
مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ [80:14]
Exalted (in dignity), kept pure and holy, [80:14]
b: elevated, in the heavens, purified, exalted above the touch of devils,

f:
بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ [80:15]
(Written) by the hands of scribes- [80:15]
b: in the hands of scribes, who write it down from the Preserved Tablet,

f:
كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ [80:16]
Honourable and Pious and Just. [80:16]
b: noble, pious, obedient to God, exalted be He: these being the angels.

f:
قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ [80:17]
Woe to man! What hath made him reject Allah; [80:17]
b: Perish man!, accursed be the disbeliever! What has made him ungrateful? (an interrogative statement meant as a rebuke) — what has driven him to disbelief?

f:
مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ [80:18]
From what stuff hath He created him? [80:18]
b: From what thing has He created him? (an interrogative meant as an affirmative, which He then explains by saying):

f:
مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ [80:19]
From a sperm-drop: He hath created him, and then mouldeth him in due proportions; [80:19]
b: From a drop of sperm did He create him then proportion him, [in stages] as a blood-clot, then an embryo up to the last [stage] of his creation.

f:
ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ [80:20]
Then doth He make His path smooth for him; [80:20]
b: Then He made the way, his exit from his mother’s belly, easy for him;

f:
ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ [80:21]
Then He causeth him to die, and putteth him in his grave; [80:21]
b: then He makes him die and buries him, He places him in a grave that hides him;

f:
ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ [80:22]
Then, when it is His Will, He will raise him up (again). [80:22]
b: then, when He wills, He will raise him, for the Resurrection.

f:
كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ [80:23]
By no means hath he fulfilled what Allah hath commanded him. [80:23]
b: No indeed! Verily, he has not accomplished, he has not done, what He, his Lord, commanded him, to [do].

f:
فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ [80:24]
Then let man look at his food, (and how We provide it): [80:24]
b: So let man consider, in reflection, his [source of] food, how it is determined and procured for him:

f:
أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا [80:25]
For that We pour forth water in abundance, [80:25]
b: that We pour down water, from the clouds, plenteously;

f:
ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا [80:26]
And We split the earth in fragments, [80:26]
b: then We split the earth into fissures, with vegetation,

f:
فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا [80:27]
And produce therein corn, [80:27]
b: and cause the grains, such as wheat and barley, to grow therein,

f:
وَعِنَبًا وَقَضْبًا [80:28]
And Grapes and nutritious plants, [80:28]
b: and vines and herbs (qadb is moist qatt),

f:
وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا [80:29]
And Olives and Dates, [80:29]
b: and olives and date-palms,

f:
وَحَدَائِقَ غُلْبًا [80:30]
And enclosed Gardens, dense with lofty trees, [80:30]
b: and gardens of dense foliage, orchards teeming with trees,

f:
وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا [80:31]
And fruits and fodder,- [80:31]
b: and fruits and pastures (abb is what cattle graze; it is also said to be ‘straw’),

f:
مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ [80:32]
For use and convenience to you and your cattle. [80:32]
b: as sustenance (understand matā‘an as mut‘atan or tamtī‘an, as explained above in the previous sūra) for you and your flocks (also as [explained] above).

f:
فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ [80:33]
At length, when there comes the Deafening Noise,- [80:33]
b: So when the [deafening] Cry, the second blast, comes —

f:
يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ [80:34]
That Day shall a man flee from his own brother, [80:34]
b: the day when a man will flee from his [own] brother,

f:
وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ [80:35]
And from his mother and his father, [80:35]
b: and his mother and his father,

f:
وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ [80:36]
And from his wife and his children. [80:36]
b: and his wife and his sons (yawma, ‘the day [when]’, is a substitution for idhā, ‘when’, the response to which is indicated by [what follows]) —

f:
لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ [80:37]
Each one of them, that Day, will have enough concern (of his own) to make him indifferent to the others. [80:37]
b: every person that day will have a matter to preoccupy him, a predicament to distract him from the affairs of others, in other words, every person will be preoccupied with his own self.

f:
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ [80:38]
Some faces that Day will be beaming, [80:38]
b: On that day some faces will be shining, radiant,

f:
ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ [80:39]
Laughing, rejoicing. [80:39]
b: laughing, joyous, happy — these are the believers.

f:
وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ [80:40]
And other faces that Day will be dust-stained, [80:40]
b: And some faces on that day will be covered with dust,

f:
تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ [80:41]
Blackness will cover them: [80:41]
b: overcast, covered, with gloom, darkness and blackness.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ [81:1]
When the sun (with its spacious light) is folded up; [81:1]
b: When the sun is folded away, enfolded and stripped of its light,

f:
وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ [81:2]
When the stars fall, losing their lustre; [81:2]
b: and when the stars scatter, [when] they are extinguished and hurtle down towards the earth,

f:
وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ [81:3]
When the mountains vanish (like a mirage); [81:3]
b: and when the mountains are set in motion, [when] they are blown away from the face of the earth, becoming as scattered dust,

f:
وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ [81:4]
When the she-camels, ten months with young, are left untended; [81:4]
b: and when the pregnant camels are neglected, abandoned without a herdsman or anyone to milk them, on account of the matter that has come over them — even though [previously] no wealth was dearer to them than these [pregnant camels];

f:
وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ [81:5]
When the wild beasts are herded together (in the human habitations); [81:5]
b: and when the wild beasts are mustered, [when they are] brought together after being resurrected so that each of them may retaliate against the other, before becoming dust;

f:
وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ [81:6]
When the oceans boil over with a swell; [81:6]
b: and when the seas are set afire (read sujirat or sujjirat), [when] they are set alight and become [a mass of] fire;

f:
وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ [81:7]
When the souls are sorted out, (being joined, like with like); [81:7]
b: and when the souls are coupled, [when they are] paired up with their bodies;

f:
وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ [81:8]
When the female (infant), buried alive, is questioned - [81:8]
b: and when the girl buried-alive, the young girl buried alive for fear of shame and impoverishment, asks — in rebuke of its slayer —

f:
بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ [81:9]
For what crime she was killed; [81:9]
b: for what sin she was slain (sa’alat, ‘asks’: a variant reading has su’ilat, ‘[she] is asked’, narrating the address directed to her, to which she then responds by saying, ‘I was slain without [having committed] any sin’);

f:
وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ [81:10]
When the scrolls are laid open; [81:10]
b: and when the scrolls, the scrolls containing the deeds, are unrolled (read nushirat or nushshirat), [when they are] unfolded and spread out;

f:
وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ [81:11]
When the world on High is unveiled; [81:11]
b: and when the heaven is stripped off, torn away from its place, just as the skin of a sheep is stripped off;

f:
وَإِذَا الْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ [81:12]
When the Blazing Fire is kindled to fierce heat; [81:12]
b: and when the Hell-fire is set ablaze (read su‘irat or su‘‘irat), [when it is] set alight;

f:
وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ [81:13]
And when the Garden is brought near;- [81:13]
b: and when Paradise is brought near, [when it is] brought close to those who have merited it, that they may enter it (the response to idhā, ‘when’, at the beginning of the sūra and all that has been supplemented thereto is [the following]):

f:
عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا أَحْضَرَتْ [81:14]
(Then) shall each soul know what it has put forward. [81:14]
b: [then] a soul, every soul, at the time of the [occurrence of the] things mentioned, which is the Day of Resurrection, will know what it has presented, of good or evil.

f:
فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ [81:15]
So verily I call to witness the planets - that recede, [81:15]
b: So I swear (fa-lā: lā is extra) by the receding [planets],

f:
الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ [81:16]
Go straight, or hide; [81:16]
b: the movers, the setters, that is, the five planets: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury (takhnusu means ‘they sink away’ during their orbit, whereas we see stars at the end of their zodiacal course return to the start; taknisu means that they enter their kinās, ‘hideaway’, in other words, they retreat into their setting-places);

f:
وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ [81:17]
And the Night as it dissipates; [81:17]
b: and [by] the night as it approaches, as it falls with its darkness, or [it means] as it recedes;

f:
وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ [81:18]
And the Dawn as it breathes away the darkness;- [81:18]
b: and [by] the dawn as it breathes, [as] it extends until it becomes broad daylight,

f:
إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ [81:19]
Verily this is the word of a most honourable Messenger, [81:19]
b: truly this, Qur’ān, is the word of a messenger [who is] noble, in the sight of God, exalted be He — this being [the messenger] Gabriel عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ (it [qawl, ‘word’] has been annexed to him, because he descends with it),

f:
ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ [81:20]
Endued with Power, with rank before the Lord of the Throne, [81:20]
b: powerful, one of mighty powers, eminent, one of eminent status (makīnin is semantically connected ‘inda, ‘in the presence of’) in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, that is, God, exalted be He;

f:
مُطَاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ [81:21]
With authority there, (and) faithful to his trust. [81:21]
b: obeyed there, the angels obey him in the heavens, trustworthy, with the Revelation.

f:
وَمَا صَاحِبُكُمْ بِمَجْنُونٍ [81:22]
And (O people!) your companion is not one possessed; [81:22]
b: And your companion, Muhammad (s) (wa-mā sāhibukum: a supplement to [the clause from] innahu, ‘truly this is’, up to the last of the oath clauses) is not a madman, as you claim.

f:
وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ [81:23]
And without doubt he saw him in the clear horizon. [81:23]
b: For verily he, Muhammad (s), saw him, Gabriel عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, in the form in which he was created, on the clear horizon, the highest one, towards the east;

f:
وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ [81:24]
Neither doth he withhold grudgingly a knowledge of the Unseen. [81:24]
b: and he, Muhammad (s), is not to be accused of [knowing] the Unseen, what is hidden of the revelation and the tidings of the heaven (a variant reading [for bi-zanīnin] has bi-danīnin, meaning that he is not ‘niggardly’ [with the Unseen] so as to reduce something of it [and not disclose it]).

f:
وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ [81:25]
Nor is it the word of an evil spirit accursed. [81:25]
b: And it, that is, the Qur’ān, is not the word of an accursed satan, eavesdropping stealthily.

f:
فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ [81:26]
When whither go ye? [81:26]
b: So where are you going? So what path are you going to follow in repudiating the Qur’ān and turning away from it?

f:
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعَالَمِينَ [81:27]
Verily this is no less than a Message to (all) the Worlds: [81:27]
b: It is only a reminder, an admonition, for all worlds, [those of] mankind and jinn,

f:
لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ [81:28]
(With profit) to whoever among you wills to go straight: [81:28]
b: for those of you who (li-man shā’a minkum is a substitution for li’l-‘ālamīna, ‘for all worlds’, using the same preposition) wish to go straight, by following the truth;

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ [82:1]
When the Sky is cleft asunder; [82:1]
b: When the heaven is split open, [when it is] rent asunder,

f:
وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ [82:2]
When the Stars are scattered; [82:2]
b: and when the stars are dispersed, [when] they expire and begin to fall,

f:
وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ [82:3]
When the Oceans are suffered to burst forth; [82:3]
b: and when the seas are burst forth, released one upon the other, forming one mass of water, so that the sweet [water] mixes with the salty;

f:
وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ [82:4]
And when the Graves are turned upside down;- [82:4]
b: and when the tombs are overturned, [when] their earth [above them] is dug up and its dead are raised (the response to idhā, ‘when’, and all that is supplemented thereto is [the following]):

f:
عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ [82:5]
(Then) shall each soul know what it hath sent forward and (what it hath) kept back. [82:5]
b: a soul, every soul, will know, at the time of the [occurrence of the] things mentioned, which is the Day of Resurrection, what it has sent ahead, in the way of deeds, and, what [it has], left behind, of these and did not do.

f:
يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ [82:6]
O man! What has seduced thee from thy Lord Most Beneficent?- [82:6]
b: O, disbelieving, man! What has deceived you with regard to your generous Lord?, so that you have disobeyed Him,

f:
الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ [82:7]
Him Who created thee. Fashioned thee in due proportion, and gave thee a just bias; [82:7]
b: Who created you, when you were not, then made you upright, in your created form, with sound limbs, then proportioned you (read fa-‘adalak or fa-‘addalak), making you symmetrical in shape, with well-proportioned parts, so that no hand or leg is longer than the other,

f:
فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ [82:8]
In whatever Form He wills, does He put thee together. [82:8]
b: assembling you in whatever (mā is a relative) form He will?

f:
كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ [82:9]
Nay! But ye do reject Right and Judgment! [82:9]
b: No indeed! — a deterrent against letting oneself be misled by the generosity of God, exalted be He. Rather you, that is, disbelievers of Mecca, deny Judgement, requital for deeds;

f:
وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ [82:10]
But verily over you (are appointed angels) to protect you,- [82:10]
b: Yet lo! there are above you watchers, from among the angels, over your deeds,

f:
كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ [82:11]
Kind and honourable,- Writing down (your deeds): [82:11]
b: noble, in God’s sight, writers, of these [deeds],

f:
يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ [82:12]
They know (and understand) all that ye do. [82:12]
b: who know whatever you do, all of it.

f:
إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ [82:13]
As for the Righteous, they will be in bliss; [82:13]
b: Indeed the pious, the believers who are sincere in their faith, shall be amid bliss, [in] Paradise,

f:
وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ [82:14]
And the Wicked - they will be in the Fire, [82:14]
b: and indeed the profligates, the disbelievers, shall be in Hell-fire, a scorching fire,

f:
يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ [82:15]
Which they will enter on the Day of Judgment, [82:15]
b: entering it, to suffer its heat, on the Day of Judgement, [the Day of] Requital,

f:
وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ [82:16]
And they will not be able to keep away therefrom. [82:16]
b: and they shall not be absent from it, [they shall not] be taken out of it.

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ [82:17]
And what will explain to thee what the Day of Judgment is? [82:17]
b: And what would show you, [what would] inform you, what the Day of Judgement is?

f:
ثُمَّ مَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ [82:18]
Again, what will explain to thee what the Day of Judgment is? [82:18]
b: Again, what would show you what the Day of Judgement is? — [repeated] to emphasise its enormity.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ [83:1]
Woe to those that deal in fraud,- [83:1]
b: Woe (waylun: a term entailing chastisement; or [it is the name of] a valley in Hell) to the defrauders:

f:
الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ [83:2]
Those who, when they have to receive by measure from men, exact full measure, [83:2]
b: those who, when they take measure from people, demand [it] in full, the measure;

f:
وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ [83:3]
But when they have to give by measure or weight to men, give less than due. [83:3]
b: but [who] when they measure for them or weigh for them, they cause [them] loss, they diminish [for them] the measure or the weight.

f:
أَلَا يَظُنُّ أُولَٰئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ [83:4]
Do they not think that they will be called to account?- [83:4]
b: Do such [individuals] not know for certain (alā indicates an interrogative of rebuke) that they will be resurrected

f:
لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ [83:5]
On a Mighty Day, [83:5]
b: for an awful day, that is to say, on it, and this is the Day of Resurrection,

f:
يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [83:6]
A Day when (all) mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds? [83:6]
b: a day when (yawma is a substitution for the [syntactical] locus of li-yawmin, ‘to an [awful] day’, and as such is in the accusative because of [the verb] mab‘ūthūna, ‘will be resurrected’) mankind will rise, from their graves, before the Lord of the Worlds?, [the Lord of] all creatures, for His affair, His reckoning and His requital.

f:
كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ [83:7]
Nay! Surely the record of the wicked is (preserved) in Sijjin. [83:7]
b: Nay!, verily, the record of the profligates, that is to say, the record of the deeds of the disbelievers, is in Sijjīn — this is said to be a book containing [the record of] all the deeds of the devils and the disbelievers; but it is also said to be a location in the lowermost part of the seventh earth, the place of Satan and his hosts.

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سِجِّينٌ [83:8]
And what will explain to thee what Sijjin is? [83:8]
b: And what would tell you what Sijjīn is?, what the book of Sijjīn is.

f:
كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ [83:9]
(There is) a Register (fully) inscribed. [83:9]
b: [It is] a sealed book.

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [83:10]
Woe, that Day, to those that deny- [83:10]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day,

f:
الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ [83:11]
Those that deny the Day of Judgment. [83:11]
b: who deny the Day of Judgement, [the Day of] Requital (alladhīna yukadhdhibūna bi-yawmi’l-dīn: either a substitution for or an explication of al-mukadhdhibīna, ‘the deniers’);

f:
وَمَا يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ [83:12]
And none can deny it but the Transgressor beyond bounds the Sinner! [83:12]
b: and none deny it but every sinful (the form [athīm] is hyperbolic) transgressor, overstepping the bounds.

f:
إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ [83:13]
When Our Signs are rehearsed to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients!" [83:13]
b: When Our signs, [of] the Qur’ān, are recited to him, he says, ‘[Mere] fables (asātīr) of the ancients!’, [mere] tales that were written down (sutirat) in ancient times (asātīr is the plural of ustūra or istāra).

f:
كَلَّا ۖ بَلْ ۜ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ [83:14]
By no means! but on their hearts is the stain of the (ill) which they do! [83:14]
b: No indeed! — a deterrent and a warning against saying such [things]. Rather there has slayed, engulfed, their hearts, covering them like rust that which they earned, of acts of disobedience.

f:
كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ [83:15]
Verily, from (the Light of) their Lord, that Day, will they be veiled. [83:15]
b: Nay!, verily, they, on that day, the Day of Resurrection, will be screened off from their Lord, and so they will not see Him.

f:
ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصَالُو الْجَحِيمِ [83:16]
Further, they will enter the Fire of Hell. [83:16]
b: Then they will be exposed to Hell-fire, [then] they will enter the scorching Fire;

f:
ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَٰذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ [83:17]
Further, it will be said to them: "This is the (reality) which ye rejected as false! [83:17]
b: then it will be said, to them: ‘This, that is, the chastisement, is that which you used to deny!’

f:
كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْأَبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ [83:18]
Day, verily the record of the Righteous is (preserved) in ´Illiyin. [83:18]
b: Nay!, verily, the record of the pious, that is, the record of the deeds of the believers who were sincere in their faith, is in ‘Illiyyūn — this is said to be the book [containing] all the good deeds of the angels and the believers from among the two heavy ones [sc. mankind and jinn]; but it is also said to be a place below the Throne in the seventh heaven;

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا عِلِّيُّونَ [83:19]
And what will explain to thee what ´Illiyun is? [83:19]
b: and what will tell you, [what will] inform you, what ‘Illiyyūn is?, what the book of ‘Illiyyūn is.

f:
كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ [83:20]
(There is) a Register (fully) inscribed, [83:20]
b: [It is] a sealed book,

f:
يَشْهَدُهُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ [83:21]
To which bear witness those Nearest (to Allah). [83:21]
b: witnessed by those brought near, from among the angels.

f:
إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ [83:22]
Truly the Righteous will be in Bliss: [83:22]
b: Assuredly the pious will be amid bliss, [in] Paradise,

f:
عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ [83:23]
On Thrones (of Dignity) will they command a sight (of all things): [83:23]
b: upon couches, [upon] beds beneath canopies, gazing, at the bliss which they have been given.

f:
تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ [83:24]
Thou wilt recognise in their faces the beaming brightness of Bliss. [83:24]
b: You will perceive in their faces the radiancy of bliss, the splendour and beauty of blissfulness,

f:
يُسْقَوْنَ مِنْ رَحِيقٍ مَخْتُومٍ [83:25]
Their thirst will be slaked with Pure Wine sealed: [83:25]
b: as they are given to drink a nectar, a wine free of any impurities, [that is] sealed, in its vessel, none other than them breaking its seal,

f:
خِتَامُهُ مِسْكٌ ۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ [83:26]
The seal thereof will be Musk: And for this let those aspire, who have aspirations: [83:26]
b: whose seal is musk, that is, whose final sip is followed by an emanating scent of musk — so for such [bliss] let the viers vie, let them desire to apply themselves to obedience of God —

f:
وَمِزَاجُهُ مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ [83:27]
With it will be (given) a mixture of Tasnim: [83:27]
b: and whose mixture, that is to say, that with which it is mixed, is of Tasnīm, which is explained by His [following] words:

f:
عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ [83:28]
A spring, from (the waters) whereof drink those Nearest to Allah. [83:28]
b: a spring (‘aynan is in the accusative because of an implicit [prefatory] amdahu, ‘I extol [this spring]’) from which those brought near will drink (yashrabu bihā: [should be yashrabu] minhā, or [it may be that bihā is used because] yashrabu is meant to imply the sense of yaltadhdhu [bihā, ‘in which they delight’]).

f:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كَانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ [83:29]
Those in sin used to laugh at those who believed, [83:29]
b: Verily the guilty, like Abū Jahl and his ilk, used to laugh at the believers, such as ‘Ammār [b. Yāsir] and Bilāl [the Ethiopian] and those like them, in mockery of them;

f:
وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ [83:30]
And whenever they passed by them, used to wink at each other (in mockery); [83:30]
b: and when they, the believers, passed them by, they would wink at one another, the guilty beckoned with their eyebrows and eyelids towards the believers in mockery;

f:
وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ [83:31]
And when they returned to their own people, they would return jesting; [83:31]
b: and when they returned to their folks they would return blithely (fākihīna: a variant reading has fakihīna), rejoicing in their [disparaging] mention of the believers;

f:
وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ [83:32]
And whenever they saw them, they would say, "Behold! These are the people truly astray!" [83:32]
b: and when they see them, that is, the believers, they say, ‘Lo! these [men] are astray!’, on account of their belief in Muhammad (s).

f:
وَمَا أُرْسِلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ [83:33]
But they had not been sent as keepers over them! [83:33]
b: God, exalted be He, says: Yet they, that is, the disbelievers, were not sent as watchers over them, [over] the believers, to preserve them or [to keep a record of] their deeds and thus guide them back to what is best for them.

f:
فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ [83:34]
But on this Day the Believers will laugh at the Unbelievers: [83:34]
b: So today, that is, the Day of Resurrection, the believers will be laughing at the disbelievers,

f:
عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ [83:35]
On Thrones (of Dignity) they will command (a sight) (of all things). [83:35]
b: upon couches, in Paradise, gazing, out from their dwellings at the disbelievers while they are being tortured; and they will laugh at them just as they, the disbelievers, had laughed at them in the world.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ [84:1]
When the sky is rent asunder, [84:1]
b: When the heaven is rent asunder,

f:
وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ [84:2]
And hearkens to (the Command of) its Lord, and it must needs (do so);- [84:2]
b: and heeds, gives ear to and, in rending itself asunder, obeys, its Lord as it should, that is, as its duty is to heed and obey,

f:
وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ [84:3]
And when the earth is flattened out, [84:3]
b: and when the earth is stretched out, [when] its width is increased, just as a piece of leather is stretched, so that no edifice or mountain remains upon it,

f:
وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ [84:4]
And casts forth what is within it and becomes (clean) empty, [84:4]
b: and casts out all that is in it, of the dead, onto its surface, and empties itself, thereof,

f:
وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ [84:5]
And hearkens to (the Command of) its Lord,- and it must needs (do so);- (then will come Home the full reality). [84:5]
b: and heeds, [and] in this respect, gives ear to and obeys, its Lord, as it should: all of this will be on the Day of Resurrection (the response to idhā, ‘when’, and [to] all that is supplemented thereto, has been omitted; but it is indicated by what follows it, and is implied to be [something like] laqiya’l-insānu ‘amalahu, ‘man will encounter his deeds’).

f:
يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ [84:6]
O thou man! Verily thou art ever toiling on towards thy Lord- painfully toiling,- but thou shalt meet Him. [84:6]
b: O man! Verily you are labouring, exerting your efforts, toward, the encounter with, your Lord, that is, death, laboriously, and you will encounter it, that is, you will encounter your mentioned good or evil deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

f:
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ [84:7]
Then he who is given his Record in his right hand, [84:7]
b: Then as for him who is given his book, the record of his deeds, in his right hand — and this is the believer —

f:
فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا [84:8]
Soon will his account be taken by an easy reckoning, [84:8]
b: he will receive an easy reckoning, which [simply] entails the presentation of his deeds to him, as in the hadīth of the two Sahīhs [of Bukhārī and Muslim] — in which there is also [a hadīth saying], ‘He who is reckoned with at length, will be destined for perdition’ — and after this presentation [of his deeds to the believer] he will be excused,

f:
وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا [84:9]
And he will turn to his people, rejoicing! [84:9]
b: and return to his family, in Paradise, joyful, because of it.

f:
وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ [84:10]
But he who is given his Record behind his back,- [84:10]
b: But as for him who is given his book from behind his back — and this is the disbeliever, whose right hand is chained to his neck and whose left hand, by which he is given the book, is placed behind his back,

f:
فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُو ثُبُورًا [84:11]
Soon will he cry for perdition, [84:11]
b: he will pray, upon seeing what is in it, for annihilation, he will invoke destruction against himself by saying: yā thabūrāh, ‘O annihilation [of mine]!’,

f:
وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا [84:12]
And he will enter a Blazing Fire. [84:12]
b: and he will enter the Blaze, an intense fire (a variant reading [for yaslā, ‘he will enter’] has yusallā, ‘he will be admitted’).

f:
إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا [84:13]
Truly, did he go about among his people, rejoicing! [84:13]
b: Indeed among his folk, his clan, in the world, he used to be joyful, wanton, lusting after his desires;

f:
إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ [84:14]
Truly, did he think that he would not have to return (to Us)! [84:14]
b: indeed he thought that (an: softened in place of the hardened form, with its subject omitted, that is to say, annahu) he would never return, to his Lord.

f:
بَلَىٰ إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا [84:15]
Nay, nay! for his Lord was (ever) watchful of him! [84:15]
b: Nay!, he will return to Him; indeed his Lord is ever Seer of him, knowing that he would return to Him.

f:
فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ [84:16]
So I do call to witness the ruddy glow of Sunset; [84:16]
b: So I swear (fa-lā: lā is extra) by the twilight (al-shafaq), the reddishness visible in the horizon after the sunset,

f:
وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ [84:17]
The Night and its Homing; [84:17]
b: and [by] the night and what it envelops, [what] it brings together of creatures and otherwise that have entered into it,

f:
وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ [84:18]
And the Moon in her fullness: [84:18]
b: and [by] the moon when it is at the full, and its light is complete, and this happens during the nights of the full moon:

f:
لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ [84:19]
Ye shall surely travel from stage to stage. [84:19]
b: you will surely journey (tarkabunna is actually tarkabūnanna, but the nūn of the indicative has been omitted because of two identical letters following one another, and the wāw [is omitted] because of two unvocalised consonants coming together), from stage to stage, state after state, namely, death, then life, then what comes afterwards of the states at the Resurrection.

f:
فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ [84:20]
What then is the matter with them, that they believe not?- [84:20]
b: So what is wrong with them, that is, the disbelievers, that they do not have faith, that is to say, what is there to prevent them from [embracing] faith; or what argument do they have for neglecting it despite the existence of proofs for it,

f:
وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْآنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ ۩ [84:21]
And when the Qur´an is read to them, they fall not prostrate, [84:21]
b: and, what is wrong with them, that when the Qur’ān is recited to them they do not prostrate?, they [do not] submit by believing in it, given its inimitability?

f:
بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُكَذِّبُونَ [84:22]
But on the contrary the Unbelievers reject (it). [84:22]
b: Nay, but the disbelievers deny, resurrection and other matters,

f:
وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ [84:23]
But Allah has full knowledge of what they secrete (in their breasts) [84:23]
b: and God knows best what they are amassing, accumulating in their scrolls, in the way of disbelief, denial and evil deeds.

f:
فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ [84:24]
So announce to them a Penalty Grievous, [84:24]
b: So give them good tidings, inform them, of a painful chastisement,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْبُرُوجِ [85:1]
By the sky, (displaying) the Zodiacal Signs; [85:1]
b: By the heaven of the constellations, the twelve constellations of the planets — as explained in [sūrat] al-Furqān [Q. 25:61];

f:
وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ [85:2]
By the promised Day (of Judgment); [85:2]
b: and [by] the promised day, the Day of Resurrection;

f:
وَشَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ [85:3]
By one that witnesses, and the subject of the witness;- [85:3]
b: and [by] the witness, Friday, and the witnessed, the day of ‘Arafa — that is how these three [elements] have been explained in hadīth: for the first one is ‘promised’, the second one is ‘a witness’ [that testifies] to deeds performed in it, while the third is ‘witnessed’ by mankind and angels (the introductory [particle] of the response to the oath has been omitted, but is implied to be laqad, ‘verily’, [sc. laqad qutila ashābu’l-ukhdūd]):

f:
قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ [85:4]
Woe to the makers of the pit (of fire), [85:4]
b: perish, accursed be, the men of the ditch!, the pit in the ground,

f:
النَّارِ ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ [85:5]
Fire supplied (abundantly) with fuel: [85:5]
b: of the fire (al-nāri is an inclusive substitution of it [al-ukhdūdi, ‘of the ditch’]), abounding in fuel, by which it was fuelled,

f:
إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ [85:6]
Behold! they sat over against the (fire), [85:6]
b: when they sat by it, around the edge of the ditch on chairs,

f:
وَهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ [85:7]
And they witnessed (all) that they were doing against the Believers. [85:7]
b: and they themselves, to what they did to those who believed, in God, in the way of torturing them by hurling [them] into the fire when they did not recant their faith, were witnesses, [they were themselves] present [thereat]. It is reported [in a hadīth] that God saved the believers who had been thrown into the fire by taking their souls before they fell into it, and that the fire then rose up and burnt all those [sitting] around it.

f:
وَمَا نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ [85:8]
And they ill-treated them for no other reason than that they believed in Allah, Exalted in Power, Worthy of all Praise!- [85:8]
b: And all that they were vindicative towards them of was that they believed in God, the Mighty, in His kingdom, the Praised,

f:
الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ [85:9]
Him to Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth! And Allah is Witness to all things. [85:9]
b: to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and God is Witness to all things, in other words, all that the disbelievers disavowed of the believers was their faith.

f:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ [85:10]
Those who persecute (or draw into temptation) the Believers, men and women, and do not turn in repentance, will have the Penalty of Hell: They will have the Penalty of the Burning Fire. [85:10]
b: Indeed those who persecute believing men and believing women, by having them burnt, then do not repent, there will be for them the chastisement of Hell, [in return] for their disbelief, and there will [also] be for them the chastisement of burning, that is to say, the chastisement for their having had the believers burnt, in the Hereafter; but it is also said [that there is this chastisement for them] in this world, as when the fire rose up and burnt them, as [mentioned] above.

f:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ [85:11]
For those who believe and do righteous deeds, will be Gardens; beneath which rivers flow: That is the great Salvation, (the fulfilment of all desires), [85:11]
b: Indeed those who believe and perform righteous deeds, for them there will be gardens underneath which rivers flow: that is the supreme triumph.

f:
إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ [85:12]
Truly strong is the Grip (and Power) of thy Lord. [85:12]
b: Assuredly your Lord’s assault, against the disbelievers, is severe, [as severe] as He will [it to be].

f:
إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ [85:13]
It is He Who creates from the very beginning, and He can restore (life). [85:13]
b: Assuredly it is He Who originates, creation, and restores, and is never thwarted in what He wills,

f:
وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ [85:14]
And He is the Oft-Forgiving, Full of Loving-Kindness, [85:14]
b: and He is the Forgiving, to sinning believers, the Loving, the One Who shows love to His friends through [His acts of] generosity,

f:
ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ [85:15]
Lord of the Throne of Glory, [85:15]
b: Lord of the Throne, its Creator and Possessor, the Glorious (read nominative al-majīdu), the One deserving of the perfect attributes of sublimity,

f:
فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ [85:16]
Doer (without let) of all that He intends. [85:16]
b: Doer of what He desires, nothing able to thwart Him.

f:
هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الْجُنُودِ [85:17]
Has the story reached thee, of the forces- [85:17]
b: Have you, O Muhammad (s), received the story of the hosts,

f:
فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ [85:18]
Of Pharaoh and the Thamud? [85:18]
b: Pharaoh and Thamūd? (Fir‘awna wa-Thamūda substitutes for al-junūdi) — the mention of ‘Pharaoh’ suffices to also include his followers; their ‘story’ is that they were destroyed for their disbelief, and this is meant as a warning for those who deny the Prophet ﷺ (s) and the Qur’ān, that they may be admonished [thereby].

f:
بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي تَكْذِيبٍ [85:19]
And yet the Unbelievers (persist) in rejecting (the Truth)! [85:19]
b: Nay, but the disbelievers are [engrossed] in denial, of the mentioned;

f:
وَاللَّهُ مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ [85:20]
But Allah doth encompass them from behind! [85:20]
b: and God is behind them, All-Encompassing — they have no protector against Him.

f:
بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ [85:21]
Day, this is a Glorious Qur´an, [85:21]
b: Nay, but it is a glorious, a magnificent, Qur’ān,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالسَّمَاءِ وَالطَّارِقِ [86:1]
By the Sky and the Night-Visitant (therein);- [86:1]
b: By the heaven and the night-visitor! (al-tāriq actually denotes any thing that comes by night, including stars, because they come out at night).

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الطَّارِقُ [86:2]
And what will explain to thee what the Night-Visitant is?- [86:2]
b: And what will tell you what the night-visitor is? (mā’l-tāriq is a subject and predicate, standing as the second object of [the verb] adrā, ‘tell’; and what comes after the first mā, ‘what’, is the predicate thereof [of this first mā]) — this [statement] emphasises the magnificence of the ‘night-visitor’, which is explained in what follows. It is:

f:
النَّجْمُ الثَّاقِبُ [86:3]
(It is) the Star of piercing brightness;- [86:3]
b: The piercing, the brilliant, because of its piercing the darkness with its light, star!, meaning [the constellation] Pleiades; or [it refers to] all stars (the response to the oath [follows]):

f:
إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ [86:4]
There is no soul but has a protector over it. [86:4]
b: Over every soul there is a keeper (if read la-mā, then mā is extra, and in, is softened in place of the hardened form with its subject omitted, that is to say, innahu; the lām is [a particle] for separation; if read lammā, then in is for negation and lammā means illā, ‘except that’) — the watcher is an angel that keeps a record of its deeds, both the good and the evil.

f:
فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ [86:5]
Now let man but think from what he is created! [86:5]
b: So let man consider, by way of reflection, from what he was created, from what thing:

f:
خُلِقَ مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ [86:6]
He is created from a drop emitted- [86:6]
b: the response is: He was created from a gushing fluid, gushing forth from the man and the woman into the womb,

f:
يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ وَالتَّرَائِبِ [86:7]
Proceeding from between the backbone and the ribs: [86:7]
b: issuing from between the loins, of the man, and the breast-bones, of the woman.

f:
إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ [86:8]
Surely (Allah) is able to bring him back (to life)! [86:8]
b: Assuredly He, exalted be He, is able to bring him back, to resurrect man after his death; and so when he reflects on his origins, he will realise that the One who was able to do this is also able to resurrect him,

f:
يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ [86:9]
The Day that (all) things secret will be tested, [86:9]
b: on the day when [all] secrets, the hidden convictions and intentions of the hearts, are inspected, [when] they are examined and revealed,

f:
فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ وَلَا نَاصِرٍ [86:10]
(Man) will have no power, and no helper. [86:10]
b: whereat he, the one who denies resurrection, will have neither strength, to defend himself against chastisement, nor any helper, to avert it from him.

f:
وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ [86:11]
By the Firmament which returns (in its round), [86:11]
b: By the heaven of returns, [of] the rain that returns time and again,

f:
وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ [86:12]
And by the Earth which opens out (for the gushing of springs or the sprouting of vegetation),- [86:12]
b: and [by] the earth of fissures, splitting with [the growth of] vegetation,

f:
إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ [86:13]
Behold this is the Word that distinguishes (Good from Evil): [86:13]
b: assuredly it, the Qur’ān, is a decisive word, distinguishing between truth and falsehood,

f:
وَمَا هُوَ بِالْهَزْلِ [86:14]
It is not a thing for amusement. [86:14]
b: and it is not a jest, frivolity or falsehood.

f:
إِنَّهُمْ يَكِيدُونَ كَيْدًا [86:15]
As for them, they are but plotting a scheme, [86:15]
b: Indeed they, that is, the disbelievers, are devising a plot, they are preparing plots against the Prophet ﷺ (s),

f:
وَأَكِيدُ كَيْدًا [86:16]
And I am planning a scheme. [86:16]
b: and I [too] am devising a plot, drawing them by degrees [towards destruction] from whence they know not.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى [87:1]
Glorify the name of thy Guardian-Lord Most High, [87:1]
b: Glorify the Name of your Lord, that is, exalt your Lord above what does not befit Him (ism [in isma rabbika, ‘the Name of your Lord’] is extra), the Most High (an adjective qualifying rabbika, ‘your Lord’),

f:
الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ [87:2]
Who hath created, and further, given order and proportion; [87:2]
b: Who created and proportioned, His creature, making it of well-proportioned parts, without irregularities,

f:
وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ [87:3]
Who hath ordained laws. And granted guidance; [87:3]
b: and Who determined, what He wants, and guided, to what He had determined of good or evil,

f:
وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعَىٰ [87:4]
And Who bringeth out the (green and luscious) pasture, [87:4]
b: and Who brought forth the pasture, [Who] caused herbage to grow,

f:
فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَاءً أَحْوَىٰ [87:5]
And then doth make it (but) swarthy stubble. [87:5]
b: then made it, after verdancy, blackened stubble, desiccated broken chaff.

f:
سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنْسَىٰ [87:6]
By degrees shall We teach thee to declare (the Message), so thou shalt not forget, [87:6]
b: We will have you recite, the Qur’ān, so that you will not forget, what you recite,

f:
إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ [87:7]
Except as Allah wills: For He knoweth what is manifest and what is hidden. [87:7]
b: except what God may will, that you forget, by abrogating its recitation and its ruling — the Prophet ﷺ (s) used to recite aloud while Gabriel عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ recited, fearing to forget, and so it is as though it was said to him, ‘Do not hasten in it; you will not forget and so do not weary yourself by reciting it aloud’; assuredly He, exalted be He, knows what is overt, of words and deeds, and what is hidden, of both of these.

f:
وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ [87:8]
And We will make it easy for thee (to follow) the simple (Path). [87:8]
b: And We will ease your way to the easy way, the uncomplicated Law, namely, Islam.

f:
فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَىٰ [87:9]
Therefore give admonition in case the admonition profits (the hearer). [87:9]
b: So remind, admonish by the Qur’ān, in case the reminder should be of benefit, to the one whom you might remind, the one mentioned in [the following verse] ‘he [who fears] will be reminded’, in other words, even if it might not be of benefit, for it is of benefit to some but of no benefit to others.

f:
سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشَىٰ [87:10]
The admonition will be received by those who fear (Allah): [87:10]
b: He who fears, God, exalted be He, will be reminded, by it, as in the verse: So admonish by the Qur’ān him who fears My threat [Q. 50:45];

f:
وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى [87:11]
But it will be avoided by those most unfortunate ones, [87:11]
b: but the wretched one (al-ashqā means al-shaqī), that is to say, the disbeliever, will shun it, that is, the reminder, in other words, he will leave it aside, not looking at it,

f:
الَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ [87:12]
Who will enter the Great Fire, [87:12]
b: he who will be roasted in the greater Fire, the Fire of the Hereafter, the lesser fire being that of this world;

f:
ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ [87:13]
In which they will then neither die nor live. [87:13]
b: then he will neither die therein, and find rest, nor live, a enjoyable life.

f:
قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّىٰ [87:14]
But those will prosper who purify themselves, [87:14]
b: Successful, winner, indeed is he who purifies himself, [who] cleanses himself by means of [his adherence to] faith,

f:
وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ [87:15]
And glorify the name of their Guardian-Lord, and (lift their hearts) in prayer. [87:15]
b: and mentions the Name of his Lord, saying Allāhu akbar, ‘God is Great’, and prays, the five prayers — and such are the concerns of [one working towards] the Hereafter, [concerns] which the Meccan disbelievers shun.

f:
بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا [87:16]
Day (behold), ye prefer the life of this world; [87:16]
b: Nay, but you prefer (or read yu’thirūna, ‘they prefer’) the life of this world, to the Hereafter,

f:
وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ [87:17]
But the Hereafter is better and more enduring. [87:17]
b: whereas the Hereafter, and the Paradise it entails, is better and more lasting.

f:
إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَىٰ [87:18]
And this is in the Books of the earliest (Revelation),- [87:18]
b: Truly this, the success of those who purify themselves, and the Hereafter being better, is in the former scrolls, the ones revealed before the Qur’ān,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ [88:1]
Has the story reached thee of the overwhelming (Event)? [88:1]
b: Has there — [there has] indeed — come to you the tiding of the Enveloper?, the Resurrection, [so called] because it ‘envelops’ creatures with its terrors.

f:
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ [88:2]
Some faces, that Day, will be humiliated, [88:2]
b: Some faces on that day — they [faces] are used to represent the individuals in both instances — will be humbled, abject,

f:
عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ [88:3]
Labouring (hard), weary,- [88:3]
b: toiling, weary, tired and exhausted from the chains and fetters,

f:
تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً [88:4]
The while they enter the Blazing Fire,- [88:4]
b: roasting (read taslā or tuslā) in a scorching fire,

f:
تُسْقَىٰ مِنْ عَيْنٍ آنِيَةٍ [88:5]
The while they are given, to drink, of a boiling hot spring, [88:5]
b: made to drink from a boiling spring, one of extremely hot temperatures.

f:
لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ [88:6]
No food will there be for them but a bitter Dhari´ [88:6]
b: They will have no food except cactus (darī‘) — a type of thorn plant which no animal grazes on because of its vileness —

f:
لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ [88:7]
Which will neither nourish nor satisfy hunger. [88:7]
b: neither nourishing, nor availing against hunger.

f:
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ [88:8]
(Other) faces that Day will be joyful, [88:8]
b: Other faces on that day will be delicate, fair,

f:
لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ [88:9]
Pleased with their striving,- [88:9]
b: pleased by their efforts, in the [life of the] world [expended] in obedience, [pleased] in the Hereafter upon seeing the reward thereof;

f:
فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ [88:10]
In a Garden on high, [88:10]
b: in a lofty Garden, [lofty] in a physical as well as an abstract sense,

f:
لَا تَسْمَعُ فِيهَا لَاغِيَةً [88:11]
Where they shall hear no (word) of vanity: [88:11]
b: in which they will not hear (read lā yusma‘u, ‘will not be heard’, or lā tasma‘u, ‘they will not hear’) any vanity, any inane soul, speaking drivel;

f:
فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ [88:12]
Therein will be a bubbling spring: [88:12]
b: therein is a running spring, of water, meaning ‘springs’;

f:
فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ [88:13]
Therein will be Thrones (of dignity), raised on high, [88:13]
b: therein are lofty couches, [lofty] in terms of their essence, their size and [physical] location,

f:
وَأَكْوَابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ [88:14]
Goblets placed (ready), [88:14]
b: and goblets, vessels without handles, set, around the edges of the springs prepared for them to drink with,

f:
وَنَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ [88:15]
And cushions set in rows, [88:15]
b: and cushions arrayed, one next to the other, against which they may lean,

f:
وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ [88:16]
And rich carpets (all) spread out. [88:16]
b: and carpets, rugs of velvet-hair, spread out.

f:
أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ [88:17]
Do they not look at the Camels, how they are made?- [88:17]
b: Will they, the Meccan disbelievers, not consider, by way of reflection, the camels, how they are created?

f:
وَإِلَى السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ [88:18]
And at the Sky, how it is raised high?- [88:18]
b: And the heaven, how it was raised?

f:
وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ [88:19]
And at the Mountains, how they are fixed firm?- [88:19]
b: And the mountains, how they were set?

f:
وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ [88:20]
And at the Earth, how it is spread out? [88:20]
b: And the earth, how it was laid out flat?, and thus infer from this the power of God, exalted be He, and His Oneness? The commencing with the [mention of] camels is because they are closer in contact with it [the earth] than any other [animal]. As for His words sutihat, ‘laid out flat’, this on a literal reading suggests that the earth is flat, which is the opinion of most of the scholars of the [revealed] Law, and not a sphere as astronomers (ahl al-hay’a) have it, even if this [latter] does not contradict any of the pillars of the Law.

f:
فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ [88:21]
Therefore do thou give admonition, for thou art one to admonish. [88:21]
b: So remind, them of God’s graces and the proofs affirming His Oneness. For you are only an admonisher;

f:
لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ [88:22]
Thou art not one to manage (men´s) affairs. [88:22]
b: you are not a taskmaster over them (a variant reading [for musaytir] has musaytir, that is to say, [not one who has been] given authority over them) — this was [revealed] before the command to struggle [against the disbelievers].

f:
إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ [88:23]
But if any turn away and reject Allah,- [88:23]
b: But he who turns away, [he who] rejects faith, and disbelieves, in the Qur’ān,

f:
فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ [88:24]
Allah will punish him with a mighty Punishment, [88:24]
b: God will chastise him with the greater chastisement, the chastisement of the Hereafter, the lesser chastisement being that of this world, that of being killed or taken captive.

f:
إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ [88:25]
For to Us will be their return; [88:25]
b: Truly to Us will be their return, their coming back after death,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالْفَجْرِ [89:1]
By the break of Day [89:1]
b: By the dawn, that is to say, [by] the dawn of each day,

f:
وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ [89:2]
By the Nights twice five; [89:2]
b: and [by] the ten nights, the [first] ten nights of Dhū’l-Hijja,

f:
وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ [89:3]
By the even and odd (contrasted); [89:3]
b: and [by] the even, the pair, and the odd (read watr or witr, two [alternative] forms), the single,

f:
وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ [89:4]
And by the Night when it passeth away;- [89:4]
b: and [by] the night in motion, falling or receding:

f:
هَلْ فِي ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ [89:5]
Is there (not) in these an adjuration (or evidence) for those who understand? [89:5]
b: Is there in that, oath, an oath for one of sense?, [one of] intellect (the response to the oath has been omitted, that is to say, [it is to be understood as something like], la-tu‘adhdhabunna yā kuffāra Makka, ‘you will assuredly be chastised O disbelievers of Mecca!’).

f:
أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ [89:6]
