Seest thou not how thy Lord dealt with the ´Ad (people),- [89:6]
b: Have you not seen, [do you not] know O Muhammad (s), how your Lord dealt with ‘Ād,

f:
إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ [89:7]
Of the (city of) Iram, with lofty pillars, [89:7]
b: Iram — these were the former [people of] ‘Ād (Irama is an explicative supplement or a substitution, and it is treated as a diptote because it is a proper noun and feminine) — of the towering ones, that is to say, the tall ones — the tallest one among them would reach four hundred cubits —

f:
الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ [89:8]
The like of which were not produced in (all) the land? [89:8]
b: the like of which was not created in the land, in terms of their power of assault and strength,

f:
وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ [89:9]
And with the Thamud (people), who cut out (huge) rocks in the valley?- [89:9]
b: and Thamūd, who hollowed, hewed, the rocks (sakhr is the plural of sakhra) in the valley, the Wādī al-Qurā, [rocks] which they used as dwellings,

f:
وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ [89:10]
And with Pharaoh, lord of stakes? [89:10]
b: and Pharaoh, the one of the tent-pegs: he used to fasten four pegs and tie to these the hands and feet of those whom he tortured —

f:
الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ [89:11]
(All) these transgressed beyond bounds in the lands, [89:11]
b: those who were rebellious, became tyrannical, in the land,

f:
فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسَادَ [89:12]
And heaped therein mischief (on mischief). [89:12]
b: and caused much corruption therein?, [by way of] slaying and otherwise.

f:
فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ [89:13]
Therefore did thy Lord pour on them a scourge of diverse chastisements: [89:13]
b: So your Lord poured on them a scourge of chastisement.

f:
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ [89:14]
For thy Lord is (as a Guardian) on a watch-tower. [89:14]
b: Assuredly your Lord is ever on the watch, watching over the deeds of servants, nothing of which escapes Him, that He may then requite them for these [deeds].

f:
فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ [89:15]
Now, as for man, when his Lord trieth him, giving him honour and gifts, then saith he, (puffed up), "My Lord hath honoured me." [89:15]
b: And as for man, the disbeliever, whenever his Lord tests him and honours him, with wealth and other things, and is gracious to him, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me’.

f:
وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ [89:16]
But when He trieth him, restricting his subsistence for him, then saith he (in despair), "My Lord hath humiliated me!" [89:16]
b: But when he tests him and restricts his provision for him, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me’.

f:
كَلَّا ۖ بَلْ لَا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ [89:17]
Nay, nay! but ye honour not the orphans! [89:17]
b: No indeed! — a disavowal [of this notion], in other words, honour is not about wealth, nor is there any humiliation in poverty, rather it has to do with obedience and disobedience [respectively]; but the disbelievers of Mecca unmindful of this. Rather they do not honour the orphan, they do not treat him with kindness, despite their wealth, or [it means that] they do not give him what is his due from an inheritance,

f:
وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ [89:18]
Nor do ye encourage one another to feed the poor!- [89:18]
b: and they do not urge, neither themselves nor others, the feeding of the needy;

f:
وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا [89:19]
And ye devour inheritance - all with greed, [89:19]
b: and they devour inheritance (turāth means mīrāth) greedily (lamman), that is to say, voraciously, when they appropriate (lammuhum) the women’s and the young ones’ share of the inheritance together with their own share of it, or to their own wealth;

f:
وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا [89:20]
And ye love wealth with inordinate love! [89:20]
b: and they love wealth with abounding love, that is to say, greatly, and so they do not expend [any] of it (a variant reading in the case of all four verbs has the second person plural).

f:
كَلَّا إِذَا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا [89:21]
Nay! When the earth is pounded to powder, [89:21]
b: No indeed! — a deterrent for them from such [conduct]. When the earth is pulverised repeatedly, when it is shaken until every edifice has collapsed and is destroyed,

f:
وَجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا [89:22]
And thy Lord cometh, and His angels, rank upon rank, [89:22]
b: and your Lord, that is to say, His command, and the angels arrive rank on rank (saffan saffan is a circumstantial qualifier, meaning ‘standing in rows’ or ‘made up of many ranks’),

f:
وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ ۚ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ الذِّكْرَىٰ [89:23]
And Hell, that Day, is brought (face to face),- on that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance profit him? [89:23]
b: and Hell on that day is brought [near], pulled by seventy thousand sets of reins, each set of reins [pulled] by the hands of seventy thousand angels, as it groans and seethes in fury; on that day (yawma’idhin is a substitution for idhā, ‘when’, the response to which is [the following]) man, that is to say, the disbeliever, will remember, his prodigal conduct in it, but how will remembering avail him [now]? (the interrogative is meant as a denial, in other words, his remembering that will not be of any use to him).

f:
يَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي [89:24]
He will say: "Ah! Would that I had sent forth (good deeds) for (this) my (Future) Life!" [89:24]
b: He will say, as he remembers: ‘O (yā is for calling attention to something) would that I had sent ahead, good deeds and faith, for my life!’, [for] a good [life] in the Hereafter, or [it means] ‘during my life’ in the world.

f:
فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ [89:25]
For, that Day, His Chastisement will be such as none (else) can inflict, [89:25]
b: Then on that day none shall mete out (read yu‘adhdhibu) His, God’s, chastisement, that is to say, He shall not delegate it to any other;

f:
وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ [89:26]
And His bonds will be such as none (other) can bind. [89:26]
b: and, likewise, none shall bind (read yūthiqu) His bind (a variant reading has yu‘adhdhabu, ‘[none] shall be chastised’, and yūthaqu, ‘[none] shall be bound’, so that the [suffixed] pronoun of ‘adhābahu and wathāqahu refers to the [chastisement and the binds of the] disbeliever, the meaning then being, ‘none shall be chastised as he shall, and none shall be bound as he shall [be bound]’).

f:
يَا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ [89:27]
(To the righteous soul will be said:) "O (thou) soul, in (complete) rest and satisfaction! [89:27]
b: ‘O soul at peace!, [the one] secure, namely, the believing one.

f:
ارْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً [89:28]
"Come back thou to thy Lord,- well pleased (thyself), and well-pleasing unto Him! [89:28]
b: Return — this is said to it upon death — to your Lord, that is to say, return to His command and to His will, pleased, with the reward, pleasing, in God’s sight with your deeds; in other words [return O soul] combining both descriptions (both of which are circumstantial qualifiers). And it will be said to it at the Resurrection:

f:
فَادْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي [89:29]
"Enter thou, then, among My devotees! [89:29]
b: Then enter among My, righteous, servants!

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَٰذَا الْبَلَدِ [90:1]
I do call to witness this City;- [90:1]
b: I swear (lā is extra) by this land, of Mecca,

f:
وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَٰذَا الْبَلَدِ [90:2]
And thou art a freeman of this City;- [90:2]
b: and you, O Muhammad (s), have free disposal of, sanction for, this land, in that you will be given permission to fight in it — and indeed God fulfilled this promise to him on the day of the Conquest [of Mecca] (thus this is a parenthetical statement intervening between that by which the oath has been sworn and that which is a supplement thereto).

f:
وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ [90:3]
And (the mystic ties of) parent and child;- [90:3]
b: And [by] the begetter, that is, Adam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, and that which he begat, that is, his descendants (mā, ‘that which’, [actually] means man, ‘whom’).

f:
لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ [90:4]
Verily We have created man into toil and struggle. [90:4]
b: We certainly created man (al-insān: the generic noun) in travail, in [a state of] toil and hardship, struggling with the tribulations of this world and the calamities of the Hereafter.

f:
أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ [90:5]
Thinketh he, that none hath power over him? [90:5]
b: Does he suppose, does the strong man of Quraysh, namely, Abū’l-Ashadd b. Kalada, presume, on account of his strength, that (an: softened in place of the hardened form, its subject omitted, that is to say, annahu) no one will have power over him? Yet God has power over him.

f:
يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالًا لُبَدًا [90:6]
He may say (boastfully); Wealth have I squandered in abundance! [90:6]
b: He says, ‘I have exhausted, in enmity of Muhammad (s), vast wealth!’, great [wealth], piles and piles of it.

f:
أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ [90:7]
Thinketh he that none beholdeth him? [90:7]
b: Does he suppose that (an, in other words, annahu) no one has seen him?, with regard to what he has expended to know the quantity thereof; God knows the quantity thereof; but it is not [in reality that much so as] to be considered a great amount, and [in any case] He will requite him for his evil conduct.

f:
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ [90:8]
Have We not made for him a pair of eyes?- [90:8]
b: Have We not given (an interrogative meant as an affirmative, in other words, ‘We have [certainly] given’) him two eyes,

f:
وَلِسَانًا وَشَفَتَيْنِ [90:9]
And a tongue, and a pair of lips?- [90:9]
b: and a tongue, and two lips,

f:
وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ [90:10]
And shown him the two highways? [90:10]
b: and guided him to the two paths?, [did We not] point out to him the path of good and that of evil?

f:
فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ [90:11]
But he hath made no haste on the path that is steep. [90:11]
b: Yet why does he not assault the obstacle?, [why] does he [not] surmount it?

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ [90:12]
And what will explain to thee the path that is steep?- [90:12]
b: And what will show you, [what will] make known to you, what the obstacle is?, that he is to surmount — intended to emphasise its enormity (this statement is a parenthetical one). He explains the way to surmount it by saying:

f:
فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ [90:13]
(It is:) freeing the bondman; [90:13]
b: the freeing of a slave, from bondage,

f:
أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ [90:14]
Or the giving of food in a day of privation [90:14]
b: or to give food on a day of hunger,

f:
يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ [90:15]
To the orphan with claims of relationship, [90:15]
b: to an orphan near of kin (maqraba means qarāba),

f:
أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ [90:16]
Or to the indigent (down) in the dust. [90:16]
b: or a needy person in misery (matraba: [literally means] ‘clinging to the dust [turāb]’ because of his poverty; a variant reading has two verbal nouns in place of the two verbs [fakka, ‘he freed’, and at‘ama, ‘he fed’], the first being in a genitive construction, fakku raqabatin, ‘the freeing of a slave’, and the second with nunation, it‘āmun, ‘to give food’, in which case there is an implied iqtihāmu before al-‘aqaba, of which the said reading becomes the explication);

f:
ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ [90:17]
Then will he be of those who believe, and enjoin patience, (constancy, and self-restraint), and enjoin deeds of kindness and compassion. [90:17]
b: while being (thumma kāna is a supplement to iqtahama, ‘he assaulted’; thumma is for the ordering of things to be mentioned) in other words, [what is meant is that] at the point of the assault he was: one of those who believe and enjoin one another to steadfastness, in [pursuing] obedience and in refraining from disobedience, and enjoin one another to compassion (marhama means rahma), towards creatures.

f:
أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ [90:18]
Such are the Companions of the Right Hand. [90:18]
b: Those, the ones described by the said attributes, are the ones of the right [side] (al-maymana means al-yamīn).

f:
وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا هُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ [90:19]
But those who reject Our Signs, they are the (unhappy) Companions of the Left Hand. [90:19]
b: But those who disbelieve in Our signs, they are the ones of the left [side] (al-mash’ama means al-shimāl).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا [91:1]
By the Sun and his (glorious) splendour; [91:1]
b: By the sun and her morning light,

f:
وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا [91:2]
By the Moon as she follows him; [91:2]
b: and [by] the moon when it follows her, rising after she has set,

f:
وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلَّاهَا [91:3]
By the Day as it shows up (the Sun´s) glory; [91:3]
b: and [by] the day when it reveals her, as it rises [high],

f:
وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا [91:4]
By the Night as it conceals it; [91:4]
b: and [by] the night when it enshrouds her, covering her up with its darkness (idhā, ‘when’, in all three instances is an absolute adverbial, operated by the verbal action of the oath).

f:
وَالسَّمَاءِ وَمَا بَنَاهَا [91:5]
By the Firmament and its (wonderful) structure; [91:5]
b: By the heaven and the One Who built it,

f:
وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا طَحَاهَا [91:6]
By the Earth and its (wide) expanse: [91:6]
b: and [by] the earth and the One Who spread it, laid out flat.

f:
وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا [91:7]
By the Soul, and the proportion and order given to it; [91:7]
b: and [by] the soul, that is to say, [by] all souls, and the One Who proportioned it, in its created form (mā in all three instances relates to the verbal action, or functions as man, ‘the one who’),

f:
فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا [91:8]
And its enlightenment as to its wrong and its right;- [91:8]
b: and inspired to discern its vices and piety, He pointed out to it the path of good and that of evil (the placing of taqwā, ‘piety’, second takes into account the [rhyme] endings of the verses; the response to the oath is [the following:])

f:
قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا [91:9]
Truly he succeeds that purifies it, [91:9]
b: Successful indeed (qad: the lām [of laqad, ‘indeed’] has been omitted from it for the sake of brevity) will be the one who purifies it, purges it of sins,

f:
وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ دَسَّاهَا [91:10]
And he fails that corrupts it! [91:10]
b: and he will indeed have failed he who eclipses it, he who obscures it with [acts of] disobedience (dassāhā is actually dassasahā, but the second sīn has been replaced with an alif for [phonetic] ease).

f:
كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَا [91:11]
The Thamud (people) rejected (their prophet) through their inordinate wrong-doing, [91:11]
b: Thamūd denied, their messenger Sālih, because of their rebellious nature,

f:
إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا [91:12]
Behold, the most wicked man among them was deputed (for impiety). [91:12]
b: when the most wretched of them, whose name was Qudār, was dispatched, [when] he hastened, in order to hamstring the she-camel with their approval.

f:
فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ نَاقَةَ اللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا [91:13]
But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "It is a She-camel of Allah! And (bar her not from) having her drink!" [91:13]
b: But then the messenger of God, Sālih, said to them, ‘[This is] the she-camel of God, so let her have her drink!’, her drink on her day — one day was hers, the next theirs.

f:
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا [91:14]
Then they rejected him (as a false prophet), and they hamstrung her. So their Lord, on account of their crime, obliterated their traces and made them equal (in destruction, high and low)! [91:14]
b: But they denied him, with regard to his saying this [as being a command] from God — which if they contravened would immediately result in chastisement being sent down on them — then hamstrung her, they slew it in order to appropriate her [share of the] drinking water. So their Lord closed in on them, the chastisement, because of their sin, and meted it equally [among them], that is, the closing in on them, in other words, He subsumed them all by it, so that not one of them escaped.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ [92:1]
By the Night as it conceals (the light); [92:1]
b: By the night as it enshrouds, with its darkness all that is between the heaven and the earth,

f:
وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ [92:2]
By the Day as it appears in glory; [92:2]
b: and [by] the day as it unveils, [as] it is revealed and becomes manifest (idhā, ‘as’, in both instances is an absolute adverbial, operated by the verbal action of the oath),

f:
وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَىٰ [92:3]
By (the mystery of) the creation of male and female;- [92:3]
b: and [by] the One Who (mā either functions as man, ‘the One Who’, or it is related to a verbal action) created the male and the female, Adam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ and Eve, or every male and female — the hermaphrodite, although problematic for us, is [in fact] either male or female according to God, and therefore a person [actually] commits perjury if he speaks with one [thinking that] because he has sworn not to speak with a male or a female; [he may do so with a hermaphrodite].

f:
إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ [92:4]
Verily, (the ends) ye strive for are diverse. [92:4]
b: Assuredly your efforts, your deeds, are dissimilar, with some working towards Paradise by means of obedience, while others [in effect] are working towards the Fire through [acts of] disobedience.

f:
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَاتَّقَىٰ [92:5]
So he who gives (in charity) and fears (Allah), [92:5]
b: As for him who gives, what is due to God, and is fearful, of God,

f:
وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ [92:6]
And (in all sincerity) testifies to the best,- [92:6]
b: and affirms the truth of the best [word], that is, [the truth] of ‘there is no god but God’ (in both places [here and below, verse 9]),

f:
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ [92:7]
We will indeed make smooth for him the path to Bliss. [92:7]
b: We shall surely ease his way to [the abode of] ease, to Paradise.

f:
وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ [92:8]
But he who is a greedy miser and thinks himself self-sufficient, [92:8]
b: But as for him who is niggardly, with what is due to God, and deems himself self-sufficient, without need for His reward, [92:9] and denies the best [word],

f:
وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ [92:9]
And gives the lie to the best,- [92:9]
b: and denies the best [word],

f:
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ [92:10]
We will indeed make smooth for him the path to Misery; [92:10]
b: We shall surely ease his way, We shall pave for him the way, to hardship, to the Fire;

f:
وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ [92:11]
Nor will his wealth profit him when he falls headlong (into the Pit). [92:11]
b: And his wealth shall not (mā is or negation) avail him when he perishes, in the Fire.

f:
إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ [92:12]
Verily We take upon Ourselves to guide, [92:12]
b: Truly with Us lies [all] guidance, the pointing out of the path of guidance from that of error, so that Our command may be followed by adhering to the former [manner of conduct] and that Our prohibition [may also be heeded] by refraining from falling into the latter [manner of conduct].

f:
وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولَىٰ [92:13]
And verily unto Us (belong) the End and the Beginning. [92:13]
b: And truly to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life], that is to say, [that of] this world, and so whoever seeks either of the two from anyone other than Us has erred.

f:
فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ [92:14]
Therefore do I warn you of a Fire blazing fiercely; [92:14]
b: So I have warned you of, I have threatened you, O people of Mecca, [with], a raging fire (talazzā, ‘raging’: one of the two original tā’ letters [of tatalazzā] has been omitted; a variant reading retains it, tatalazzā, that is, ‘one that is flaming’),

f:
لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى [92:15]
None shall reach it but those most unfortunate ones [92:15]
b: which none shall enter but the wretched one (al-ashqā means al-shaqī),

f:
الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ [92:16]
Who give the lie to Truth and turn their backs. [92:16]
b: he who denies, the Prophet ﷺ, and turns away, from faith — this delimiting [of those who deserve to enter this fire] constitutes an interpretation of His saying, But He forgives other than that to whomever He will [Q. 4:48], which in turn suggests that what is meant is that entry [into the Fire] which will be everlasting.

f:
وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى [92:17]
But those most devoted to Allah shall be removed far from it,- [92:17]
b: The God-fearing one (al-atqā means al-taqī) shall be spared it, he will be removed far away from it,

f:
الَّذِي يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ [92:18]
Those who spend their wealth for increase in self-purification, [92:18]
b: he who gives his wealth to purify himself, offering it as a [means of self] purification before God, exalted be He, by making this payment for the sake of God, exalted be He, and not for show or the sake of reputation, so that he [or the offering] stands purified in the sight of God. This [verse] was revealed regarding the truthful one (al-siddīq) [Abū Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ], may God be pleased with him, when he purchased Bilāl [the Ethiopian], who was being tortured on account of his faith, and then freed him, whereat the disbelievers said, ‘He only did this in return for a favour which he [must have] owed him’, and so the following was revealed:

f:
وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ [92:19]
And have in their minds no favour from anyone for which a reward is expected in return, [92:19]
b: and no one has any favour [outstanding] with him that must be requited;

f:
إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَىٰ [92:20]
But only the desire to seek for the Countenance of their Lord Most High; [92:20]
b: but, he did this, only seeking the pleasure of his Lord the Most High, that is to say, only seeking [to secure] God’s reward;

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالضُّحَىٰ [93:1]
By the Glorious Morning Light, [93:1]
b: By the forenoon, that is to say, the first part of the day or all of it,

f:
وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ [93:2]
And by the Night when it is still,- [93:2]
b: and [by] the night when it is still — or [sajā can mean] ‘when it envelops [all] in its darkness’.

f:
مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ [93:3]
Thy Guardian-Lord hath not forsaken thee, nor is He displeased. [93:3]
b: Your Lord has neither forsaken you, He has [not] abandoned you, O Muhammad (s), nor does He hate you: this was revealed when, after the revelation had not come to him for fifteen days, the disbelievers said, ‘His Lord has parted with him and hates him’.

f:
وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ [93:4]
And verily the Hereafter will be better for thee than the present. [93:4]
b: And verily the Hereafter shall be better for you, by virtue of the honours awaiting you thereat, than the first [life], this world.

f:
وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ [93:5]
And soon will thy Guardian-Lord give thee (that wherewith) thou shalt be well-pleased. [93:5]
b: And verily your Lord shall give you, in the Hereafter, of good things, a bounteous gift, and you shall be satisfied, with it — and so the Prophet ﷺ (s) said, ‘In that case, I shall not be satisfied if a single person from among my community remains in the Fire’ (the response to the oath terminates here, with two affirmations and two negations).

f:
أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَىٰ [93:6]
Did He not find thee an orphan and give thee shelter (and care)? [93:6]
b: Did He not find you an orphan (an interrogative meant as an affirmative, in other words, He did [indeed] find you [an orphan]), having lost your father before you were born or [shortly] thereafter, and shelter you?, by having your uncle Abū Tālib embrace you [as part of his household].

f:
وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ [93:7]
And He found thee wandering, and He gave thee guidance. [93:7]
b: And did He not find you erring, from the [revealed] Law which you [now] follow, and guided you?, that is, and then guided you to it.

f:
وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ [93:8]
And He found thee in need, and made thee independent. [93:8]
b: And did He not find you needy, poor, and enrich you?, [and] made you content with the spoils and other things which He gave you — in a hadīth [it is stated], ‘Wealth comes not from the proliferation of transient [worldly] goods, but wealth comes from the contentedness of the soul’.

f:
فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ [93:9]
Therefore, treat not the orphan with harshness, [93:9]
b: So, as for the orphan, do not oppress [him], by appropriating his wealth or otherwise,

f:
وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ [93:10]
Nor repulse the petitioner (unheard); [93:10]
b: and as for the beggar, do not drive [him] away, [do not] repel him on account of his poverty,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ [94:1]
Have We not expanded thee thy breast?- [94:1]
b: Did We not expand (an interrogative meant as an affirmative, in other words, ‘We did [indeed] expand’) your breast for you, O Muhammad (s), by means of prophethood and otherwise,

f:
وَوَضَعْنَا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ [94:2]
And removed from thee thy burden [94:2]
b: and relieve you of your burden,

f:
الَّذِي أَنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ [94:3]
The which did gall thy back?- [94:3]
b: that which weighed down your back? — this is similar to where God says: that God may forgive you what is past of your sin [Q. 48:2].

f:
وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ [94:4]
And raised high the esteem (in which) thou (art held)? [94:4]
b: Did We not exalt your mention? For you are mentioned where I [God] am mentioned in the call announcing [the time for] prayer (adhān), in the [second] call to perform the prayer (iqāma), in the witnessing [‘there is no god but God, Muhammad is His Messenger’] (tashahhud), in the Friday sermon and in other instances.

f:
فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا [94:5]
So, verily, with every difficulty, there is relief: [94:5]
b: For truly with hardship comes ease.

f:
إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا [94:6]
Verily, with every difficulty there is relief. [94:6]
b: Truly with hardship comes ease: the Prophet ﷺ (s) suffered much hardship at the hands of the disbelievers, but then he enjoyed ease when he was assisted to victory [by God] over them.

f:
فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَانْصَبْ [94:7]
Therefore, when thou art free (from thine immediate task), still labour hard, [94:7]
b: So when you are finished, from [performing] prayer, toil, exert yourself in supplication [to God],

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالتِّينِ وَالزَّيْتُونِ [95:1]
By the Fig and the Olive, [95:1]
b: By the fig and the olive, that is, the two [edible] foods — or [these denote the names of] two mountains in Syria on which these two foods grow —

f:
وَطُورِ سِينِينَ [95:2]
And the Mount of Sinai, [95:2]
b: and [by] the Mount Sinai, the mountain on which God, exalted be He, spoke to Moses عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ (sīnīn means ‘the one blessed’ or ‘the fair one with fruitful trees’),

f:
وَهَٰذَا الْبَلَدِ الْأَمِينِ [95:3]
And this City of security,- [95:3]
b: and [by] this secure land: Mecca, as people were secure in it in the time of pagandom and [are still secure in it] in Islam.

f:
لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ [95:4]
We have indeed created man in the best of moulds, [95:4]
b: Verily We created man (al-insān: the generic) in the best of forms, [in the best] proportioning of his shape.

f:
ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ [95:5]
Then do We abase him (to be) the lowest of the low,- [95:5]
b: Then, in the case of certain individuals of his [species], We reduced him to the lowest of the low — a metaphor for old age and weakness, at which point a believer’s deeds are fewer than when he was young; but he will still have his reward, as God, exalted be He, says:

f:
إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ [95:6]
Except such as believe and do righteous deeds: For they shall have a reward unfailing. [95:6]
b: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds, for they shall have an unfailing reward, one unending — in a hadīth [it is stated], ‘When a believer reaches that stage of old age which prevents him from performing [good] deeds, then what he used to do is recorded in his favour [instead]’.

f:
فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ [95:7]
Then what can, after this, contradict thee, as to the judgment (to come)? [95:7]
b: So what makes you deny, O disbeliever, thereafter — after the mention of man being created in the best of forms and his being reduced to the vilest of age, all of which indicates the power [of God] to resurrect — the Judgement?, the Requital that will be preceded by the Resurrection and the Reckoning. In other words, what makes you disbelieve in all this? Nothing does!

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ [96:1]
Proclaim! (or read!) in the name of thy Lord and Cherisher, Who created- [96:1]
b: Recite, bring recitation into existence, beginning with: In the Name of your Lord Who created, all creatures;

f:
خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ [96:2]
Created man, out of a (mere) clot of congealed blood: [96:2]
b: created man (al-insān: the generic) from a blood-clot (‘alaq is the plural of ‘alaqa, which is a small quantity of congealing blood).

f:
اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ [96:3]
Proclaim! And thy Lord is Most Bountiful,- [96:3]
b: Recite: (reiterating the first one) and your Lord is the Most Generous, having no counterpart in terms of His generosity (wa-rabbuka’l-akram is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject [of the verb] iqra’, ‘recite’),

f:
الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ [96:4]
He Who taught (the use of) the pen,- [96:4]
b: Who taught, [the art of] script, by the pen — the first to write with it was [the prophet] Enoch (Idrīs), peace be upon him —

f:
عَلَّمَ الْإِنْسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ [96:5]
Taught man that which he knew not. [96:5]
b: taught man (al-insān: the generic) what he did not know, before he was taught, in the way of guidance, [the art of] writing, crafts and so on.

f:
كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ [96:6]
Day, but man doth transgress all bounds, [96:6]
b: Nay, but verily man is [wont to be] rebellious,

f:
أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنَىٰ [96:7]
In that he looketh upon himself as self-sufficient. [96:7]
b: when he sees it, that is to say, his own soul, to be self-sufficient, in terms of wealth — this was revealed regarding Abū Jahl (ra’ā, ‘sees’, means [to see] mentally; istaghnā, ‘self-sufficient’, is the second direct object; an ra’āhu, ‘when he sees it’, is an object denoting reason).

f:
إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَىٰ [96:8]
Verily, to thy Lord is the return (of all). [96:8]
b: Surely to your Lord, O man, is the return — [meant as] a threat for him — and so He will requite the rebellious one with what he deserves.

f:
أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ [96:9]
Seest thou one who forbids- [96:9]
b: Have you seen (a-ra’ayta in all three instances [here and below] is an exclamation of wonder) him, namely, Abū Jahl, who forbids

f:
عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّىٰ [96:10]
A votary when he (turns) to pray? [96:10]
b: a servant, namely, Muhammad (s), when he prays?

f:
أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰ [96:11]
Seest thou if he is on (the road of) Guidance?- [96:11]
b: Have you considered what if he, the one forbidden, should be upon [a path of] guidance,

f:
أَوْ أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوَىٰ [96:12]
Or enjoins Righteousness? [96:12]
b: or (aw is for division) be bidding [others] to fear of God?

f:
أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ [96:13]
Seest thou if he denies (Truth) and turns away? [96:13]
b: Have you considered what if he, the one forbidding the Prophet ﷺ, should be denying [God’s guidance] and turning away?, from faith.

f:
أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَىٰ [96:14]
Knoweth he not that Allah doth see? [96:14]
b: Is he not aware that God sees?, what has issued from him, that is to say, He does [indeed] know it and will requite him for it. In other words, ‘Marvel, O you being addressed, at the way in which he forbids prayer, and at the fact that the one being forbidden is actually the one upon guidance, bidding to fear of God, while the one forbidding is a denier, disregarding faith’.

f:
كَلَّا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ [96:15]
Let him beware! If he desist not, We will drag him by the forelock,- [96:15]
b: No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Assuredly if (la-in: the lām is for oaths) he does not desist, from the disbelief that he is upon, We shall seize him by the forelock, We shall drag him to the Fire by his forelock,

f:
نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ [96:16]
A lying, sinful forelock! [96:16]
b: a lying, iniquitous forelock! (nāsiyatin: an indefinite noun substituting for a definite) — the description of this [forelock] in such terms is meant figuratively, and what is actually meant is that individual.

f:
فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ [96:17]
Then, let him call (for help) to his council (of comrades): [96:17]
b: Let him, then, call upon [the henchmen of] his council, the members of his council (nādin) — a place of assembly where people gather to talk. He [Abū Jahl] had said to the Prophet ﷺ (s) in reproof, having forbidden him from prayer, ‘You are well aware that there is none in this [town] who has [recourse to] as large a council [of men] as I do. Verily, I shall fill this [entire] valley with mature steeds and young men [in battle] against you if you so wish!’

f:
سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ [96:18]
We will call on the angels of punishment (to deal with him)! [96:18]
b: We shall call the Zabāniya, the grim stern angels to destroy him, as [stated] in the hadīth, ‘Had he called his council [of henchmen] together, the Zabāniya would have seized him right before his own eyes!’.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ [97:1]
We have indeed revealed this (Message) in the Night of Power: [97:1]
b: Lo! We revealed it, that is, the Qur’ān, in its entirety, [sending it down] from the Preserved Tablet to the heaven of this world, on the Night of Ordainment, that is, [the Night] of great eminence.

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ [97:2]
And what will explain to thee what the night of power is? [97:2]
b: And what will show you, [what] will make known to you, O Muhammad (s), what the Night of Ordainment is? — [intended] to emphasise its great status and to provoke marvel at it.

f:
لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ [97:3]
The Night of Power is better than a thousand months. [97:3]
b: The Night of Ordainment is better than a thousand months, in which there is no Night of Ordainment, for a righteous deed on that Night is better than one [performed] for a thousand months without it.

f:
تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ [97:4]
Therein come down the angels and the Spirit by Allah´s permission, on every errand: [97:4]
b: The angels and the Spirit, namely, Gabriel عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, descend (tanazzalu: one of the two original tā’ letters [of tatanazzalu] has been omitted) in it, on that night, by the leave of their Lord, by His command, with every command, that God has decreed from that year to the following one (min is causative functioning as bi, ‘with’).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ [98:1]
Those who reject (Truth), among the People of the Book and among the Polytheists, were not going to depart (from their ways) until there should come to them Clear Evidence,- [98:1]
b: The disbelievers from among (min: explicative) the People of the Scripture and the idolaters, that is, the idol-worshippers (wa’l-mushrikīna is a supplement to ahl, ‘the People of’) were not going to leave off (munfakkīna is the predicate of yakun, ‘were’), that is to say, they were not going to abandon their ways, until the clear proof, namely, Muhammad (s), should come to them, that is, [until] it came to them;

f:
رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً [98:2]
An messenger from Allah, rehearsing scriptures kept pure and holy: [98:2]
b: a messenger from God (rasūlun mina’Llāhi substitutes for al-bayyinatu, ‘the clear proof’), namely, the Prophet ﷺ (s), reciting pages purified, of [all] falsehood,

f:
فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ [98:3]
Wherein are laws (or decrees) right and straight. [98:3]
b: wherein are upright precepts, written rulings that are upright, that is to say, one who recites what contains all that, and that is the Qur’ān. Thus some of them believed in it, while others disbelieved.

f:
وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ [98:4]
Nor did the People of the Book make schisms, until after there came to them Clear Evidence. [98:4]
b: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided, regarding belief in him [the Prophet ﷺ] (s), except after the clear proof had come to them, namely, the Prophet ﷺ (s) — or the Qur’ān which he brought as his miracle. Before his (s) arrival they had all agreed to believe in him when he would come; then those who disbelieved in him from among them became envious of him.

f:
وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ [98:5]
And they have been commanded no more than this: To worship Allah, offering Him sincere devotion, being true (in faith); to establish regular prayer; and to practise regular charity; and that is the Religion Right and Straight. [98:5]
b: And they were only commanded, in their Scripture, the Torah and the Gospel, to worship God (illā li-ya‘budū means illā an ya‘budū, an having been omitted and the lām added) devoting religion purely to Him, [free] of any idolatry, as hanīfs, upright in [following] the religion of Abraham عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ and the religion of Muhammad (s), when he would come — so how is it that they disbelieved in him?, and to establish prayer and pay the alms. That is the upright religion, the upright creed.

f:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ [98:6]
Those who reject (Truth), among the People of the Book and among the Polytheists, will be in Hell-Fire, to dwell therein (for aye). They are the worst of creatures. [98:6]
b: Truly the disbelievers from among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters shall be in the fire of Hell, to abide therein (khālidīna: an implied circumstantial qualifier, in other words, it will be decreed for them by God, exalted be He, to abide therein) — those are the worst of creatures.

f:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ [98:7]
Those who have faith and do righteous deeds,- they are the best of creatures. [98:7]
b: Truly those who believe and perform righteous deeds — they are the best of creatures (al-bariyya means al-khalīqa).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا [99:1]
When the earth is shaken to her (utmost) convulsion, [99:1]
b: When earth is shaken, [when] it is rocked for the rising of the Hour, with its [final] quake, with its most violent rocking, one that befits its magnitude,

f:
وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا [99:2]
And the earth throws up her burdens (from within), [99:2]
b: and the earth brings forth its burdens, its hidden treasures and its dead, casting them onto its surface,

f:
وَقَالَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا لَهَا [99:3]
And man cries (distressed): ´What is the matter with her?´- [99:3]
b: and man, the disbeliever in resurrection, says, ‘What is wrong with it?’ — in denial of that situation.

f:
يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا [99:4]
On that Day will she declare her tidings: [99:4]
b: On that day (yawma’idhin substitutes for, and is the response to, idhā, ‘when’) it shall relate its chronicles, it shall inform of the good and evil deeds committed in it,

f:
بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا [99:5]
For that thy Lord will have given her inspiration. [99:5]
b: for its Lord will have inspired it, that is, He will have commanded her to [do] this — in a hadīth [it is stated], ‘It [the earth] shall testify to every single deed committed by every servant and handmaiden upon its surface’.

f:
يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًا لِيُرَوْا أَعْمَالَهُمْ [99:6]
On that Day will men proceed in companies sorted out, to be shown the deeds that they (had done). [99:6]
b: On that day mankind shall issue forth, they will depart from the site of the Reckoning, in separate groups, divided up, so that those taking it [their book] by the right hand will go to Paradise, while those taking it by the left hand will go to the Fire, to be shown their deeds, that is, the requital for them, in [either] Paradise or the Fire.

f:
فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ [99:7]
Then shall anyone who has done an atom´s weight of good, see it! [99:7]
b: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good shall see it: he shall see its reward,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحًا [100:1]
By the (Steeds) that run, with panting (breath), [100:1]
b: By the chargers, the steeds that charge in attack and snort [with a], snorting — this being the [name of the] sound which they emit from inside them when they charge;

f:
فَالْمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحًا [100:2]
And strike sparks of fire, [100:2]
b: by the strikers, the steeds that strike fire [by way], of sparks, with their hoofs, when they gallop across rocky terrain by night;

f:
فَالْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحًا [100:3]
And push home the charge in the morning, [100:3]
b: by the dawn-raiders, the steeds that make raids against the enemy at dawn at the hands of their riders,

f:
فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا [100:4]
And raise the dust in clouds the while, [100:4]
b: raising, stirring up, therein, in the place of their charge or at that time [of dawn], a trail of dust, by the power of their movement,

f:
فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا [100:5]
And penetrate forthwith into the midst (of the foe) en masse;- [100:5]
b: cleaving therewith, with the dust, a host, of the enemy, that is to say, cutting right into their centre! (the verb is supplemented to the noun [in the above instances] because it serves to explain the verbal action, in other words, wa’llātī ‘adawna fa-awrayna fa-agharna, ‘by those that charge, then strike sparks, then raid’).

f:
إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ [100:6]
Truly man is, to his Lord, ungrateful; [100:6]
b: Verily man, the disbeliever, is ungrateful to his Lord, thankless, denying [the reality of] His graces, exalted be He,

f:
وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ [100:7]
And to that (fact) he bears witness (by his deeds); [100:7]
b: and verily to that, ingratitude of his, he is a witness, bearing witness against himself to his own actions.

f:
وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ [100:8]
And violent is he in his love of wealth. [100:8]
b: And verily in the love of wealth he is avid, and is therefore niggardly with it.

f:
أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ [100:9]
Does he not know,- when that which is in the graves is scattered abroad [100:9]
b: Does he not know that, when that which is in the graves, in the way of the dead, is strewn, when it is turned over and brought out, that is to say, [that when] they are raised,

f:
وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ [100:10]
And that which is (locked up) in (human) breasts is made manifest- [100:10]
b: and that which is in the breasts, the hearts, of disbelief or faith, is obtained, [when] it is revealed and examined,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْقَارِعَةُ [101:1]
The (Day) of Noise and Clamour: [101:1]
b: The Clattering Blow, the Resurrection that will make hearts clatter by its terrors.

f:
مَا الْقَارِعَةُ [101:2]
What is the (Day) of Noise and Clamour? [101:2]
b: What is the Clattering Blow? — [intended] to emphasise its awesomeness (mā’l-qāri‘a: both of these [elements] constitute a subject and a predicate, and [together] the predicate of [the first] al-qāri‘a).

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ [101:3]
And what will explain to thee what the (Day) of Noise and Clamour is? [101:3]
b: And what will show you, [what] will make known to you, what the Clattering Blow is? — additional emphasis of its awesomeness (the first mā is a subject, and what follows it is its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function together as the second direct object of [the verb] adrā, ‘show’).

f:
يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ [101:4]
(It is) a Day whereon men will be like moths scattered about, [101:4]
b: The day (yawma: that which renders it accusative is [the verb] indicated by al-qāri‘a, in other words, [by the implied] taqra‘u, ‘it clatters’) mankind will be like scattered moths, like a throng of scattered locusts surging into each other in confusion, until they are summoned to the Reckoning,

f:
وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ [101:5]
And the mountains will be like carded wool. [101:5]
b: and the mountains will be like tufts of wool, like carded wool in terms of the lightness with which it floats [in the air] until it comes to settle upon the earth.

f:
فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ [101:6]
Then, he whose balance (of good deeds) will be (found) heavy, [101:6]
b: Then as for him whose scales weigh heavy, in that his good deeds outweigh his misdeeds,

f:
فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ [101:7]
Will be in a life of good pleasure and satisfaction. [101:7]
b: he will enjoy a pleasant life, in Paradise, that is to say, a pleasing one, for he will be pleased with it, that is, it will be pleasing to him;

f:
وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ [101:8]
But he whose balance (of good deeds) will be (found) light,- [101:8]
b: but as for him whose scales weigh light, in that his evil deeds outweigh his good ones,

f:
فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ [101:9]
Will have his home in a (bottomless) Pit. [101:9]
b: his home will be the Abyss.

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ [101:10]
And what will explain to thee what this is? [101:10]
b: And what will show you what it is?, that is to say, what the Abyss is.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ [102:1]
The mutual rivalry for piling up (the good things of this world) diverts you (from the more serious things), [102:1]
b: Rivalry [in worldly things], mutual vainglory about wealth, children and men, distracts you, preoccupies you [diverting you] from obedience to God,

f:
حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ [102:2]
Until ye visit the graves. [102:2]
b: until you visit the graves, [either] in that you have died and then been buried in them, or [it means] to the extent that you [actually] count the dead as a something to rival one another by.

f:
كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ [102:3]
But nay, ye soon shall know (the reality). [102:3]
b: No indeed! — a disavowal. You will come to know!

f:
ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ [102:4]
Again, ye soon shall know! [102:4]
b: Again, no indeed! You will come to know, the evil consequences of your mutual vainglory at the moment of the extraction [of the soul], then [you will come to know] in the grave.

f:
كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ [102:5]
Nay, were ye to know with certainty of mind, (ye would beware!) [102:5]
b: No indeed! — verily — Were you to know with certain knowledge, the consequences of your vainglory, you would not preoccupy yourselves with it, [for]

f:
لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ [102:6]
Ye shall certainly see Hell-Fire! [102:6]
b: you would surely see hell-fire, the Fire (la-tarawunna’l-jahīma: this is the response to an omitted oath; the third consonant of the root of the verb [r-’-y] together with the second have been omitted, and its vowel has been transposed onto the rā’).

f:
ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ [102:7]
Again, ye shall see it with certainty of sight! [102:7]
b: Again, you will surely see it — [repeated] for emphasis — with the eye of certainty (‘ayna is a verbal noun, as both ra’ā and ‘āyana have the same meaning).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالْعَصْرِ [103:1]
By (the Token of) Time (through the ages), [103:1]
b: By Time! — or [it ‘asr can mean the period] from the declining of the sun to sunset, or [it may denote] the afternoon prayer.

f:
إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ [103:2]
Verily Man is in loss, [103:2]
b: Verily man (al-insān: the generic) is in [a state of] loss, in all his bargaining,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ [104:1]
Woe to every (kind of) scandal-monger and-backbiter, [104:1]
b: Woe (waylun: an expression implying chastisement) to every backbiter, [who is a] slanderer, frequently engaging in backbiting and slander, that is to say, defamation — this was revealed regarding those who slandered the Prophet ﷺ (s) and the believers, the likes of Umayya b. Khalaf, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra and others —

f:
الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ [104:2]
Who pileth up wealth and layeth it by, [104:2]
b: who amasses (read jama‘a or jamma‘a) wealth and counts it over, keeping count of it and stores it aside as a provision against the [unforeseeable] calamities of time.

f:
يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ [104:3]
Thinking that his wealth would make him last for ever! [104:3]
b: He thinks, in his ignorance, that his wealth will make him immortal, never to die.

f:
كَلَّا ۖ لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ [104:4]
By no means! He will be sure to be thrown into That which Breaks to Pieces, [104:4]
b: Nay! — a repudiation — He will surely be flung (la-yunbadhanna is the response to an omitted oath), that is, he will be hurled down, into the Crusher, that crushes everything that is thrown into it.

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ [104:5]
And what will explain to thee That which Breaks to Pieces? [104:5]
b: And what will show you, [what] will make known to you, what the Crusher is?

f:
نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ [104:6]
(It is) the Fire of (the Wrath of) Allah kindled (to a blaze), [104:6]
b: [It is] the fire of God, kindled, set ablaze,

f:
الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ [104:7]
The which doth mount (Right) to the Hearts: [104:7]
b: which peers over the hearts, to burn them — the pain of which is much more severe than any other because of the delicate nature [of the heart].

f:
إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ [104:8]
It shall be made into a vault over them, [104:8]
b: Lo! it will be closed in (mu’sada or mūsada) on them (‘alayhim, ‘on them’: the plural pronoun takes into account the [plural] import of kull, ‘every’),

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ [105:1]
Seest thou not how thy Lord dealt with the Companions of the Elephant? [105:1]
b: Have you not considered (an interrogative meant to provoke marvel, in other words, ‘marvel at’) the way in which your Lord dealt with the Men of the Elephant?, who was named Mahmūd, and the men were Abraha, King of Yemen and his troops. He had built a church in San‘ā’ in order to divert pilgrims away from Mecca to it. A man from among the Banū Kināna defecated in it and stained its prayer niche with a deflowered virgin’s blood, in contempt of it. Abraha then swore that he would knock down the Ka‘ba. So he approached Mecca with his troops riding Yemeni elephants with Mahmūd at the vanguard. But when they turned to destroy the Ka‘ba, God unleashed upon them what He relates in His words:

f:
أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ [105:2]
Did He not make their treacherous plan go astray? [105:2]
b: Did He not make — that is to say, He did [indeed] make — their stratagem, to destroy the Ka‘ba, go astray, [ending up] in failure and destruction,

f:
وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ [105:3]
And He sent against them Flights of Birds, [105:3]
b: and unleashed upon them swarms of birds, [birds] in droves, one following the next (it is said there is no singular form for it [abābīl], like asātīr; but some say that the singular is abūl or ibāl or ibbīl, similar [in constructed pattern] to ‘ajūl, miftāh and sikkīn),

f:
تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ [105:4]
Striking them with stones of baked clay. [105:4]
b: pelting them with stones of baked clay,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ [106:1]
For the covenants (of security and safeguard enjoyed) by the Quraish, [106:1]
b: [In gratitude] for the security of Quraysh,

f:
إِيلَافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ [106:2]
Their covenants (covering) journeys by winter and summer,- [106:2]
b: their security (īlāfihim: repeated for emphasis; it is a verbal noun from [the verb] ālafa) for the journey of winter, to Yemen, and, the journey, of summer, to Syria, every year: they made use of these two journeys to provide for their trade at the station [of Abraham عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ] in Mecca, in order to attend to the House [of God], which was their source of pride; they [Quraysh] were the descendants of al-Nadr b. Kināna;

f:
فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَٰذَا الْبَيْتِ [106:3]
Let them adore the Lord of this House, [106:3]
b: let them worship (fa’l-ya‘budū is semantically connected to li-ilāfi, ‘for the security’, the fā’ being extra) the Lord of this House,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ [107:1]
Seest thou one who denies the Judgment (to come)? [107:1]
b: Have you seen him who denies the Judgement?, the Requital and the Reckoning, that is to say, ‘Do you know who he is?’ If you do not know him then:

f:
فَذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ [107:2]
Then such is the (man) who repulses the orphan (with harshness), [107:2]
b: That is he (read an implied huwa after the fā’ [of fa-dhālika]) who repels the orphan, that is to say, [who] violently drives him away from what is his due,

f:
وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ [107:3]
And encourages not the feeding of the indigent. [107:3]
b: and does not urge, either himself or others [to], the feeding of the needy: this was revealed regarding al-‘Āsī b. Wā’il or al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.

f:
فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ [107:4]
So woe to the worshippers [107:4]
b: So woe to them who pray,

f:
الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ [107:5]
Who are neglectful of their prayers, [107:5]
b: those who are heedless of their prayers, neglectful, delaying them from their appointed times,

f:
الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ [107:6]
Those who (want but) to be seen (of men), [107:6]
b: those who make a pretence, with prayers and otherwise,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ [108:1]
To thee have We granted the Fount (of Abundance). [108:1]
b: We have assuredly given you, O Muhammad (s), Abundance — [the name of] a river in Paradise and his [the Prophet’s ﷺ] pool around which his community shall gather; al-kawthar also means the abundant good [that has been given to the Prophet ﷺ], such as prophethood, the Qur’ān, intercession, and the like.

f:
فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ [108:2]
Therefore to thy Lord turn in Prayer and Sacrifice. [108:2]
b: So pray to your Lord, the prayer of the Festival of Immolation (‘īd al-nahr), and sacrifice, your offering.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ [109:1]
Say : O ye that reject Faith! [109:1]
b: Say: ‘O disbelievers!

f:
لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ [109:2]
I worship not that which ye worship, [109:2]
b: I do not worship, at present, what you worship, of idols,

f:
وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ [109:3]
Nor will ye worship that which I worship. [109:3]
b: and you do not worship, at present, what I worship, and that is God, exalted be He, alone,

f:
وَلَا أَنَا عَابِدٌ مَا عَبَدْتُمْ [109:4]
And I will not worship that which ye have been wont to worship, [109:4]
b: nor will I worship, in the future, what you have worshipped,

f:
وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ [109:5]
Nor will ye worship that which I worship. [109:5]
b: nor will you worship, in the future, what I worship: God knew that they would never become believers (the use of [the inanimate] mā, ‘what’, to refer to God is meant to counter [the reference to ‘what thing’ they worship]).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ [110:1]
When comes the Help of Allah, and Victory, [110:1]
b: When the help of God, for His Prophet (s), against his enemies, comes together with victory, the victory over Mecca,

f:
وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا [110:2]
And thou dost see the people enter Allah´s Religion in crowds, [110:2]
b: and you see people entering God’s religion, that is to say, Islam, in throngs, in large droves, after they had been entering one by one — this was after the conquest of Mecca, when the Arabs from all corners of the land came to him willingly [in obedience to his command] —

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ [111:1]
Perish the hands of the Father of Flame! Perish he! [111:1]
b: Perish, ruined be, the hands of Abū Lahab, in other words, all of him — the use of ‘hands’ here to denote [all of] him is figurative, and is because most actions are performed by them; the statement is an invocation — and perish he!, may he be ruined! (this [tabba] is a predicate, as where one says, ahlakahu’Llāhu wa-qad halak, ‘God destroyed him and he indeed is destroyed’. When the Prophet ﷺ threatened him with the chastisement, he said, ‘If what my brother’s son says is true, then I shall ransom [myself] from it with my wealth and sons!’; so the following was revealed:

f:
مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ [111:2]
No profit to him from all his wealth, and all his gains! [111:2]
b: His wealth will not avail him, nor what he has earned (wa-kasab means wa-kasbihi, that is to say, his sons; mā aghnā means [mā] yughnī).

f:
سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ [111:3]
Burnt soon will he be in a Fire of Blazing Flame! [111:3]
b: He will [soon] enter a Fire of flames, that is to say, [a fire that is] flaming and ignited (this [statement] is the source of his nickname, [which was given to him] on account of his flaming reddish fair face),

f:
وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ [111:4]
His wife shall carry the (crackling) wood - As fuel!- [111:4]
b: and his wife (wa’mra’atuhu is a supplement to the person [of the verb] yaslā, ‘he will enter’, separated by the clause of the direct object and its qualification) — and this was Umm Jamīl — the carrier (read hammālatu or hammālata) of firewood, cactus and thorns which she used to fling into the path of the Prophet ﷺ (s).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ [112:1]
Say: He is Allah, the One and Only; [112:1]
b: Say: ‘He is God, One (Allāhu is the predicate of huwa, ‘He is’, and ahadun is its substitution or a second predicate).

f:
اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ [112:2]
Allah, the Eternal, Absolute; [112:2]
b: God, the Self-Sufficient, Besought of all (Allāhu’l-samad constitute a subject and a predicate) [al-samad means] the One Who is always sought at times of need,

f:
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ [112:3]
He begetteth not, nor is He begotten; [112:3]
b: He neither begot, for no likeness of Him can exist, nor was begotten, since createdness is precluded in His case.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ [113:1]
Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the Dawn [113:1]
b: Say: ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak, the morning,

f:
مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ [113:2]
From the mischief of created things; [113:2]
b: from the evil of what He has created, of obligated animate beings and non-obligated ones and from all inanimates, such as poison and so on;

f:
وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ [113:3]
From the mischief of Darkness as it overspreads; [113:3]
b: and from the evil of darkness when it gathers, that is, [from] night when it becomes dark and the moon when it is absent,

f:
وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ [113:4]
From the mischief of those who practise secret arts; [113:4]
b: and from the evil of the women-blowers, sorceresses who blow, on knots, which they knot into strings, blowing into them [certain] words, but without spittle; however, al-Zamakhsharī says, ‘with this [spittle]’ — [sorceresses] such as the daughters of the said Labīd —

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ [114:1]
Say: I seek refuge with the Lord and Cherisher of Mankind, [114:1]
b: Say: ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, their Creator and their Possessor: they [mankind] have been singled out for mention here in order to honour them, and a preface to seeking refuge from the evil of the one who whispers in their hearts;

f:
مَلِكِ النَّاسِ [114:2]
The King (or Ruler) of Mankind, [114:2]
b: the King of mankind,

f:
إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ [114:3]
The god (or judge) of Mankind,- [114:3]
b: the God of mankind (both [maliki’l-nās and ilāhi’l-nās] are either substitutions or adjectival qualifications or explicative supplements; the repetition of the annexed word [al-nās] is meant as an additional explication),

f:
مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ [114:4]
From the mischief of the Whisperer (of Evil), who withdraws (after his whisper),- [114:4]
b: from the evil of the slinking whisperer, Satan — he is referred to by the name of the action [waswasa] on account of his repeated engaging in it — who slinks [away] and recoils from the heart whenever God is mentioned,

f:
الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ [114:5]
(The same) who whispers into the hearts of Mankind,- [114:5]
b: who whispers in the breasts of mankind, in their hearts — whenever they neglect to remember God,
